sentences.zh: 【唐紀四十八】起旃蒙赤奮若八月，盡強圉單閼七月，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 48] From Zhanmeng Chifenruo, eighth month, through Qiangyu Shanyan, seventh month; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 48] The span runs from the eighth month of Zhanmeng Chifenruo through the seventh month of Qiangyu Shanyan—two years in all.

translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong of Tang, seventh reign year, first year of Zhenyuan (

sentences.zh: 乙丑，公元七八五年）

translations.literal: yichou, 785 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yichou, AD 785)

sentences.zh: 八月，甲子，詔凡不急之費及人冗食者皆罷之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiazi, an edict ordered that all non-urgent expenditures and redundant offices with superfluous staff be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day jiazi, an edict abolished every nonessential expense and every post burdened with redundant personnel.

sentences.zh: 馬燧至行營，與諸將謀曰：「長春宮不下，則懷光不可得。

translations.literal: Ma Sui arrived at the field headquarters and said to the generals in council: "If Changchun Palace is not taken, Huai'guang cannot be captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Sui reached the field headquarters, he told the generals in council, "Unless we take Changchun Palace, we will never get Huai'guang.

sentences.zh: 長春宮守備甚嚴，攻之曠日持久，我當身往諭之。」

translations.literal: Changchun Palace's defenses are very strict; an assault would drag on for days. I shall go in person to persuade them."
translations.idiomatic: Changchun Palace is heavily defended, and an assault would drag on for days. I will go there myself and talk them around."

sentences.zh: 遂徑造城下，呼懷光守將徐庭光，庭光帥將士羅拜城上。

translations.literal: He then went straight to the foot of the wall and called out to Huai'guang's defending general Xu Tingguang; Tingguang led his officers and men in ranks to bow on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: With that he went straight to the foot of the wall and called up to Huai'guang's defender Xu Tingguang, who lined his officers and men along the ramparts and bowed to him in ranks.

sentences.zh: 燧知其心屈，徐謂之曰：「我自朝廷來，可西向受命。」

translations.literal: Sui knew their hearts were yielding and said slowly to them: "I have come from the court; you may face west to receive orders."
translations.idiomatic: Sui could see their will was breaking. He said calmly, "I have come from the court. Face west and receive your orders."

sentences.zh: 庭光等復西向拜。

translations.literal: Tingguang and the others again bowed facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Tingguang and the others bowed westward again.

sentences.zh: 燧曰：「汝曹自祿山已來，徇國立功四十餘年，何忽為滅族之計！

translations.literal: Sui said: "You have served the state and won merit for more than forty years since the time of Lushan—why suddenly plot the extermination of your clans!
translations.idiomatic: Sui said, "Since the days of Lushan you have served the state and won merit for more than forty years. Why turn now to a course that will wipe out your families?

sentences.zh: 從吾言，非止免禍，富貴可圖也。」

translations.literal: Follow my words, and you will not only escape disaster—wealth and rank can be secured."
translations.idiomatic: Do as I say, and you will not only escape ruin—you can still win wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 眾不對。

translations.literal: The crowd did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered.

sentences.zh: 燧披襟曰：「汝不信吾言，何不射我！」

translations.literal: Sui opened his robe and said: "If you do not believe me, why not shoot me!"
translations.idiomatic: Sui threw open his robe. "If you do not believe me," he said, "why not shoot me?"

sentences.zh: 將士皆伏泣。

translations.literal: The officers and men all prostrated themselves and wept.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and men all prostrated themselves and wept.

sentences.zh: 燧曰：「此皆懷光所為，汝曹無罪。

translations.literal: Sui said: "All of this is Huai'guang's doing; you are not guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Sui said, "All of this is Huai'guang's doing. You are not guilty.

sentences.zh: 第堅守勿出。」

translations.literal: Only hold firm and do not come out."
translations.idiomatic: Just hold the walls and do not come out."

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: They all said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: They all said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 壬申，燧與渾瑊、韓游瑰軍逼河中，至焦籬堡。

translations.literal: On renshen, Sui advanced with the armies of Hun Jian and Han Yougui against Hezhong and reached Jiaoli Fort.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Sui marched with the armies of Hun Jian and Han Yougui against Hezhong and came to Jiaoli Fort.

sentences.zh: 守將尉珪以七百人降。

translations.literal: The defending general Wei Gui surrendered with seven hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: The defending general Wei Gui surrendered with seven hundred men.

sentences.zh: 是夕，懷光舉火，諸營不應。

translations.literal: That evening Huai'guang raised signal fires, but the camps did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: That night Huai'guang lit signal fires, but none of the camps answered.

sentences.zh: 駱元光在長春宮下，使人招徐庭光。

translations.literal: Luo Yuanguang was below Changchun Palace and sent someone to summon Xu Tingguang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yuanguang was camped below Changchun Palace and sent a man to summon Xu Tingguang.

sentences.zh: 庭光素輕元光，遣卒罵之，又為優胡於城上以侮之，且曰：「我降漢將耳！」

translations.literal: Tingguang had always looked down on Yuanguang; he sent soldiers to revile him and also staged a Hu clown play on the wall to mock him, saying: "I will surrender only to a Han general!"
translations.idiomatic: Tingguang had always despised Yuanguang. He sent soldiers to curse him, staged a Hu clown play on the wall to mock him, and said, "I will surrender only to a Han general!"

sentences.zh: 元光使白燧，燧還至城下，庭光開門降。

translations.literal: Yuanguang had someone inform Sui; Sui returned to the foot of the wall, and Tingguang opened the gate and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguang sent word to Sui, who returned to the foot of the wall. Tingguang opened the gate and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 燧以數騎入城慰撫，其眾大呼曰：「吾輩復為王人矣！」

translations.literal: Sui entered the city with a few horsemen to reassure them; the troops shouted: "We are subjects of the king again!"
translations.idiomatic: Sui entered the city with a few horsemen to reassure the garrison, and the men shouted, "We are the emperor's men again!"

sentences.zh: 渾瑊謂僚佐曰：「始吾謂馬公用兵不吾遠也，今乃知吾不逮多矣！」

translations.literal: Hun Jian said to his staff: "At first I thought Lord Ma's use of troops was not far from mine; now I know I fall far short!"
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian told his staff, "At first I thought Lord Ma's way of war was not far from mine. Now I see how far short I fall!"

sentences.zh: 詔以庭光試殿中監兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Tingguang acting Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Tingguang acting Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，燧帥諸軍至河西，河中軍士自相驚曰：「西城擐甲矣！」

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Sui led the armies to the west of the river; the Hezhong soldiers alarmed one another, saying: "The western city is donning armor!"
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Sui led the armies to the west bank of the river. The Hezhong troops panicked one another, crying, "They are arming on the western wall!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「東城娖隊矣！」

translations.literal: Then they said: "The eastern city is forming ranks!"
translations.idiomatic: Then they cried, "They are forming ranks on the eastern wall!"

sentences.zh: 須臾，軍中皆易其號為「太平」字。

translations.literal: In a moment the whole army changed its battle cry to the character "Peace."
translations.idiomatic: In a moment the whole army had changed its battle cry to "Peace."

sentences.zh: 懷光不知所為，乃縊而死。

translations.literal: Huai'guang did not know what to do and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang did not know what to do and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 初，懷光之解奉天圍也，上以其子璀為監察御史，寵待甚厚。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huai'guang had lifted the siege of Fengtian, the emperor made his son Cui a supervising censor and treated him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Huai'guang had lifted the siege of Fengtian, the emperor had made his son Cui a supervising censor and treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 及懷光屯咸陽不進，璀密言於上曰：「臣父必負陛下，願早為之備。

translations.literal: When Huai'guang encamped at Xianyang and would not advance, Cui said secretly to the emperor: "My father is certain to betray Your Majesty; I beg you to prepare early.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'guang camped at Xianyang and would not advance, Cui told the emperor in secret, "My father is sure to betray you. Please prepare while there is still time.

sentences.zh: 臣聞君、父一也，但今日之勢，陛下未能誅臣父，而臣父足以危陛下。

translations.literal: I have heard that lord and father are one, but in today's situation Your Majesty cannot execute my father, while my father is fully able to endanger Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I know that sovereign and father are one in principle, but in today's situation you cannot kill my father, while my father can still endanger you.

sentences.zh: 陛下待臣厚，臣胡人，性直，故不忍不言耳。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has treated me generously; I am a Hu by birth and blunt by nature, so I cannot bear not to speak."
translations.idiomatic: You have treated me generously. I am a Hu by birth and blunt by nature, so I could not keep silent."

sentences.zh: 上驚曰：「知卿大臣愛子，當為朕委曲彌縫，而密奏之！」

translations.literal: The emperor said in alarm: "Knowing you are a great minister's beloved son, you should smooth things over for me in private and report secretly!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said in alarm, "Knowing you are a great minister's beloved son, you should smooth things over for me in private and report in secret!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣父非不愛臣，臣非不愛其父與宗族也；

translations.literal: He replied: "My father does not fail to love me, nor do I fail to love my father and clan;
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "My father does love me, and I do love my father and my clan.

sentences.zh: 顧臣力竭，不能回耳。」

translations.literal: only my strength is exhausted and I cannot turn him back."
translations.idiomatic: But my strength is spent, and I cannot turn him back."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然則卿以何策自免？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Then by what plan will you save yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then how do you plan to save yourself?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣之進言，非苟求生，臣父敗，則臣與之俱死矣，復有何策哉！

translations.literal: He replied: "My speaking out was not to seek life at any price; if my father falls, I shall die with him—what plan is there!
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I did not speak out merely to save my own skin. If my father falls, I will die with him. What plan could there be?

sentences.zh: 使臣賣父求生，陛下亦安用之！」

translations.literal: If I were to sell out my father to live, would Your Majesty employ me!"
translations.idiomatic: If I sold out my father to live, would you still want me?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿勿死，為朕更至咸陽諭卿父，使君臣父子俱全，不亦善乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do not die; go again to Xianyang for me and persuade your father, so that lord and minister, father and son, may all be preserved—is that not good!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Do not die. Go again to Xianyang for me and persuade your father, so that sovereign and minister, father and son, may all be preserved. Would that not be best?"

sentences.zh: 璀至咸陽而還，曰：「無益也，願陛下備之，勿信人言。

translations.literal: Cui went to Xianyang and returned, saying: "It is useless; I beg Your Majesty to prepare and not believe what people say.
translations.idiomatic: Cui went to Xianyang and returned. "It is no use," he said. "Please prepare, and do not believe what people tell you.

sentences.zh: 臣今往，說諭萬方，臣父言：『汝小子何知！

translations.literal: I have just gone and argued every way I could; my father said: 'You little fool, what do you know!
translations.idiomatic: I have just gone and argued every way I could. My father said, 'You little fool—what do you know?

sentences.zh: 主上無信，吾非貪寶貴也，直畏死耳，汝豈可陷吾入死地邪！』

translations.literal: The sovereign is faithless; I do not crave treasure and rank—I only fear death. How can you trap me in a place of death!'
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign is faithless. I am not greedy for treasure and rank—I only fear death. How can you trap me in a place of death?'

sentences.zh: 」及李泌赴陝，上謂之曰：「朕所以再三欲全懷光者，誠惜璀也。

translations.literal: " When Li Bi went to Shan, the emperor said to him: "The reason I repeatedly wished to spare Huai'guang was truly that I pitied Cui.
translations.idiomatic: " When Li Bi went to Shan, the emperor told him, "The reason I kept trying to spare Huai'guang was that I pitied Cui.

sentences.zh: 卿至，試為朕招之。」

translations.literal: When you arrive, try to summon him for me."
translations.idiomatic: When you arrive, try to bring him in for me."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下未幸梁、洋，懷光猶可降也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Before Your Majesty took refuge at Liang and Yang, Huai'guang could still have submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Before you took refuge at Liang and Yang, Huai'guang might still have submitted.

sentences.zh: 今則不然，豈有人臣迫逐其君，而可復立於其朝乎！

translations.literal: Now it is not so—can a subject who drove his lord into flight stand again in that court!
translations.idiomatic: That is no longer possible. How can a subject who drove his sovereign into flight stand again in that court?

sentences.zh: 縱彼顏厚無慚，陛下每視朝，何心見之！

translations.literal: Even if he were shameless, how could Your Majesty face him at every audience!
translations.idiomatic: Even if he were shameless, how could you bear to see him at every audience?

sentences.zh: 臣得入陝，借使懷光請降，臣不敢受，況招之乎！

translations.literal: If I reach Shan and Huai'guang should ask to surrender, I would not dare accept it—how much less summon him!
translations.idiomatic: If I reach Shan and Huai'guang asks to surrender, I would not dare accept it—how much less summon him!

sentences.zh: 李璀固賢者，必與父俱死矣，若其不死，則亦無足貴也。」

translations.literal: Li Cui is indeed a worthy man and will surely die with his father; if he did not die, he would not be worth honoring."
translations.idiomatic: Li Cui is a worthy man and will surely die with his father. If he did not, he would not be worth honoring anyway."

sentences.zh: 及懷光死，璀先刃其二弟，乃自殺。

translations.literal: When Huai'guang died, Cui first cut down his two younger brothers and then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'guang died, Cui first killed his two younger brothers and then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 朔方將牛名俊斷懷光首出降。

translations.literal: The Shuofang general Niu Mingjun cut off Huai'guang's head and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Shuofang general Niu Mingjun cut off Huai'guang's head and came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 河中兵猶萬六千人，燧斬其將閻晏等七人，餘皆不問。

translations.literal: The Hezhong army still numbered sixteen thousand; Sui executed seven of its generals, including Yan Yan, and questioned no one else.
translations.idiomatic: The Hezhong army still numbered sixteen thousand men. Sui executed seven of its generals, including Yan Yan, and questioned no one else.

sentences.zh: 燧自辭行至河中平，凡二十七日。

translations.literal: From the time Sui took leave to march until Hezhong was pacified was twenty-seven days in all.
translations.idiomatic: From the day Sui set out until Hezhong was pacified took twenty-seven days in all.

sentences.zh: 燧出高郢、李鄘於獄，皆奏置幕下。

translations.literal: Sui released Gao Ying and Li Yong from prison and memorialized to place both in his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Sui released Gao Ying and Li Yong from prison and memorialized to place both on his staff.

sentences.zh: 韓游瑰之攻懷光也，楊懷賓戰甚力，上命特原其子朝晟，游環遂以朝晟為都虞侯。

translations.literal: When Han Yougui attacked Huai'guang, Yang Huaibin fought very fiercely; the emperor ordered his son Chaocheng specially pardoned, and Yougui then made Chaocheng chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Yougui attacked Huai'guang, Yang Huaibin fought with great vigor. The emperor ordered his son Chaocheng specially pardoned, and Yougui then made Chaocheng chief adjutant.

sentences.zh: 上使問陸贄：「河中既平，復有何事所宜區處？」

translations.literal: The emperor sent to ask Lu Zhi: "Now that Hezhong is pacified, what further matters ought to be arranged?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent to ask Lu Zhi, "Now that Hezhong is pacified, what further matters ought to be arranged?"

sentences.zh: 令悉條奏。

translations.literal: He ordered him to set everything out in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him to set everything out in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 贄以河中既平，慮必有希旨生事之人，以為王師所向無敵，請乘勝討淮西者。

translations.literal: Zhi, because Hezhong was pacified, feared there would be men eager to please by stirring up trouble, claiming the imperial armies were invincible wherever they marched and urging a victorious advance against Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hezhong was pacified, Zhi feared that flatterers would stir up trouble, claiming the imperial armies were invincible and urging a victorious advance against Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 李希烈必誘諭其所部及新附諸帥曰：「奏天息兵之旨，乃因窘急而言，朝廷稍安，必復誅伐。」

translations.literal: Li Xilie would surely entice and instruct his subordinates and the newly submitted commanders, saying: "The edict to cease arms at Fengtian was spoken only in distress; once the court is a little settled, it will surely punish again."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie would surely tell his subordinates and the newly submitted commanders, "The edict to cease arms at Fengtian was spoken only in distress. Once the court is a little settled, it will punish us again."

sentences.zh: 如此，則四方負罪者孰不自疑，河朔、青齊固當響應，兵連禍結，賦役繁興，建中之憂，行將復起。

translations.literal: In this way, who among the guilty throughout the realm would not grow suspicious; Heshuo and Qingqi would surely respond in turn; war would link with disaster, levies and corvée would multiply, and the troubles of the Jianzhong era would soon rise again.
translations.idiomatic: Then every guilty man in the realm would grow suspicious, Heshuo and Qingqi would surely rise in turn, war would link with disaster, levies and corvée would multiply, and the troubles of the Jianzhong era would soon return.

sentences.zh: 乃上奏，其略曰：』福不可以屢徼，幸不可以常覬。」

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial, in summary saying: "Fortune cannot be sought again and again; luck cannot be constantly counted on."
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial that said, in summary, "Fortune cannot be courted again and again, and luck cannot be counted on forever."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣姑以生禍為憂，而未敢以獲福為賀。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Your servant ventures to worry about fresh disaster and does not yet dare to congratulate on gained fortune."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Your servant ventures to worry about fresh disaster and does not yet dare to congratulate you on gained fortune."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陛下懷悔過之深誠，降非常之大號，所在宣揚之際，聞者莫不涕流。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your Majesty bears deep sincerity of repentance and has issued an extraordinary great proclamation; wherever it was proclaimed, none who heard it failed to weep.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Your Majesty bears deep repentance and has issued an extraordinary proclamation. Wherever it was proclaimed, none who heard it failed to weep.

sentences.zh: 假王叛換之夫，削偽號以請罪。

translations.literal: Men who had borrowed royal titles in rebellion cast off their false designations to beg pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Men who had taken royal titles in rebellion cast off their false designations to beg pardon.

sentences.zh: 觀釁首鼠之次，一純誠以效勤。」

translations.literal: Watching for openings, they wavered like mice at a threshold, then with single-hearted sincerity offered their service."
translations.idiomatic: Watching for openings, they wavered like mice at a threshold, then offered their service with single-hearted sincerity."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「曩討之而愈叛，今釋之而畢來。

translations.literal: He also said: "Before, when they were punished they rebelled all the more; now, when they are released, they all come in.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Before, when they were punished they rebelled all the more; now, when they are released, they all come in.

sentences.zh: 曩以百萬之師而力殫，今以咫尺之詔而化洽。

translations.literal: Before, a million troops exhausted their strength; now, a proclamation within a foot's reach brings universal harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Before, a million troops exhausted their strength; now, a proclamation within arm's reach brings universal harmony.

sentences.zh: 是則聖王之敷理道，服暴人，任德而不任兵，明矣；

translations.literal: Thus it is clear that the sage king spreads the Way of governance, subdues violent men, and relies on virtue rather than arms;
translations.idiomatic: This shows clearly that the sage king spreads the Way of governance, subdues violent men, and relies on virtue rather than arms.

sentences.zh: 群帥之悖臣禮，拒天誅，圖活而不圖王，又明矣。

translations.literal: it is equally clear that the commanders violated the minister's rites, defied heaven's punishment, and sought life rather than kingship.
translations.idiomatic: It is equally clear that the commanders violated the minister's rites, defied heaven's punishment, and sought life rather than kingship.

sentences.zh: 是則好生以及物者，乃自生之方；

translations.literal: Thus cherishing life and extending it to others is the method of preserving one's own life;
translations.idiomatic: Cherishing life and extending it to others is the way to preserve one's own life.

sentences.zh: 施安以及物者，乃自安之術。

translations.literal: bestowing peace and extending it to others is the art of securing one's own peace.
translations.idiomatic: Bestowing peace and extending it to others is the art of securing one's own peace.

sentences.zh: 擠彼於死地而求此之久生也，措彼於危地而求此之久安也，從古及今，未之有焉。」

translations.literal: To drive others to death and seek long life for oneself, to place others in peril and seek lasting peace for oneself—from antiquity to the present there has never been such a thing."
translations.idiomatic: To drive others to death and seek long life for yourself, to place others in peril and seek lasting peace for yourself—from antiquity to the present there has never been such a thing."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「一夫不率，闔境罹殃；

translations.literal: He also said: "When one man does not lead aright, the whole region suffers calamity;
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "When one man does not lead aright, the whole region suffers calamity.

sentences.zh: 一境不寧，普天致擾。」

translations.literal: when one region is not at peace, the whole realm is thrown into turmoil."
translations.idiomatic: When one region is not at peace, the whole realm is thrown into turmoil."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「億兆污人，四三叛帥，感陛下自新之旨，悅陛下盛德之言，革面易辭，且修臣禮，其於深言密議固亦未盡坦然，必當聚心而謀，傾耳而聽，觀陛下所行之事，考陛下所誓之言。

translations.literal: He also said: "The myriad people were stained; three or four rebel commanders, moved by Your Majesty's call to renew yourselves and pleased by Your Majesty's words of great virtue, changed their faces and altered their speech and began to observe the minister's rites—yet in their secret counsels they are surely not fully at ease; they must gather their hearts to plot and incline their ears to listen, watching what Your Majesty does and testing what Your Majesty has sworn.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The myriad people were stained, and three or four rebel commanders, moved by your call to renew yourselves and pleased by your words of great virtue, changed their faces and altered their speech and began to observe the minister's rites. Yet in their secret counsels they are surely not fully at ease. They will gather their hearts to plot and incline their ears to listen, watching what you do and testing what you have sworn.

sentences.zh: 若言與事符，則遷善之心漸固；

translations.literal: If words match deeds, the heart to turn toward good will gradually firm;
translations.idiomatic: If words match deeds, the heart to turn toward good will gradually firm.

sentences.zh: 儻事與言背，則慮禍之態復興。」

translations.literal: if deeds contradict words, the mood of fearing disaster will rise again."
translations.idiomatic: If deeds contradict words, the mood of fearing disaster will rise again."

sentences.zh: 又「朱泚滅而懷光戮，懷光戮而希烈征，希烈儻平，禍將次及，則彼之蓄素疑而懷宿負者，能不為之動心哉！」

translations.literal: He also said: "Zhu Ci was destroyed and Huai'guang executed; Huai'guang executed and Xilie campaigned against—if Xilie should be pacified, disaster will reach them next; then those who have long nursed suspicion and old grievances—can they fail to be stirred!"
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Zhu Ci was destroyed and Huai'guang executed; Huai'guang executed and Xilie campaigned against. If Xilie should be pacified, disaster will reach them next. Then those who have long nursed suspicion and old grievances—can they fail to be stirred?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「今皇運中興，天禍將悔，以逆泚之偷居上國，以懷光之竊保中畿，歲未再周，相次梟殄，實眾慝驚心之日，群生改觀之時。

translations.literal: He also said: "Now the imperial fortune is reviving at its midpoint and heaven's disaster is about to repent; the rebel Ci usurped the upper realm and Huai'guang clung to the central capital—within less than two years they were executed in succession. This is truly the day when the multitude of evils are startled at heart and the people change how they look on things.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Now the imperial fortune is reviving and heaven's disaster is turning back. The rebel Ci usurped the upper realm and Huai'guang clung to the central capital—within less than two years they were executed in succession. This is truly the day when evildoers are startled at heart and the people change how they look on things.

sentences.zh: 威則已行，惠猶未洽。

translations.literal: Might has already been shown, but grace is not yet fully spread.
translations.idiomatic: Might has already been shown, but grace has not yet fully spread.

sentences.zh: 誠宜上副天眷，下收物情，布恤人之惠以濟威，乘滅賊之威以行惠。」

translations.literal: It is truly fitting to answer heaven's favor above and gather the people's feelings below—to spread the grace that comforts men to balance might, and use the might that destroyed the rebels to carry out grace."
translations.idiomatic: It is truly fitting to answer heaven's favor above and win the people's hearts below—to spread the grace that comforts men to balance might, and use the might that destroyed the rebels to carry out grace."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣所未敢保其必從，唯希烈一人而已。

translations.literal: He also said: "What your servant does not dare guarantee will surely follow is only Xilie alone.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "What I do not dare guarantee will surely follow is only Xilie alone.

sentences.zh: 揆其私心，非不願從也；

translations.literal: Judging his private heart, he is not unwilling to submit;
translations.idiomatic: Judging his private heart, he is not unwilling to submit.

sentences.zh: 想其潛慮，非不追悔也。

translations.literal: considering his hidden thoughts, he is not without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Considering his hidden thoughts, he is not without regret.

sentences.zh: 但以猖狂失計，已竊大號，雖荷陛下全宥之恩，然不能不自面見於天地之間耳。

translations.literal: Only because he lost his wits in rashness and has already usurped the great title, though he owes Your Majesty full pardon, he cannot but feel shame before heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Only because he lost his wits in rashness and has already usurped the great title, though he owes you full pardon, he cannot but feel shame before heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 縱未順命，斯為獨夫，內則無辭以起兵，外則無類以求助，其計不過厚撫部曲，偷容歲時，心雖陸梁，勢必不致。

translations.literal: Even if he does not obey orders, he is a lone man; within he has no grounds to raise troops, without he has no ally to seek aid; his plan can be no more than richly comforting his troops and stealing years of respite—his heart may be defiant, but the situation will surely not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he does not obey orders, he is a lone man. Within he has no grounds to raise troops; without he has no ally to seek aid. His plan can be no more than richly comforting his troops and stealing years of respite. His heart may be defiant, but the situation will surely not allow it.

sentences.zh: 陛下但敕諸鎮各守封疆，彼既氣奪算窮，是乃狴牢之類，不有人禍，則當鬼誅。

translations.literal: Your Majesty need only order the various circuits each to hold its borders; once his spirit is broken and his schemes exhausted, he is of the kind kept in a prison—if no human disaster strikes, ghostly punishment will.
translations.idiomatic: You need only order the various circuits each to hold its borders. Once his spirit is broken and his schemes exhausted, he is a man in a cage—if no human disaster strikes, ghostly punishment will.

sentences.zh: 古之不戰而屈人之兵者，斯之謂歟！

translations.literal: Of old, subduing another's army without fighting—this is what is meant!
translations.idiomatic: Of old they spoke of subduing another's army without fighting—this is what they meant!

sentences.zh: 丁卯，詔以「李懷光嘗有功，宥其一男，使續其後，賜之田宅，歸其首及屍使葬。

translations.literal: On dingmao, an edict stated: "Li Huai'guang once had merit; spare one of his sons to continue his line, grant him fields and a residence, and return his head and corpse for burial.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, an edict stated, "Li Huai'guang once had merit. Spare one of his sons to continue his line, grant him fields and a residence, and return his head and corpse for burial.

sentences.zh: 加馬燧兼侍中，渾瑊檢校司空，餘將卒賞賚各有差。

translations.literal: Ma Sui was promoted to concurrent Palace Attendant; Hun Jian was made acting Minister of Works; the remaining officers and soldiers received rewards in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui was promoted to concurrent Palace Attendant, Hun Jian was made acting Minister of Works, and the remaining officers and soldiers received rewards in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 諸道與淮西連接者，宜各守封疆，非彼侵軼，不須進討。

translations.literal: The circuits bordering Huaixi should each hold its borders; unless the other side encroaches, there is no need to advance in attack.
translations.idiomatic: The circuits bordering Huaixi should each hold its borders. Unless the other side encroaches, there is no need to advance in attack.

sentences.zh: 李希烈若降，當待以不死，自餘將士百姓，一無所問。」

translations.literal: If Li Xilie submits, he shall be treated so that he does not die; as for the rest of the officers, soldiers, and common people, none shall be questioned."
translations.idiomatic: If Li Xilie submits, he shall be spared death. As for the rest of the officers, soldiers, and common people, none shall be questioned."

sentences.zh: 初，李晟嘗將神策軍戍成都，及還，以營妓高洪自隨。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Sheng had once led the Shence Army to garrison Chengdu; on his return he took with him the camp courtesan Gao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Sheng had once led the Shence Army to garrison Chengdu. On his return he took with him the camp courtesan Gao Hong.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使張延賞怒，追而還之，由是有隙。

translations.literal: The Xichuan military governor Zhang Yanshang was angry, pursued and recovered her, and from this a rift arose.
translations.idiomatic: The Xichuan military governor Zhang Yanshang was angry, pursued her, and recovered her. From this a rift arose.

sentences.zh: 至是，劉從一有疾，上召延賞入相。

translations.literal: At this time Liu Congyi fell ill, and the emperor summoned Yanshang to enter the government as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Liu Congyi fell ill, and the emperor summoned Yanshang to enter the government as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 晟表陳其過惡，上重違其意，以延賞為左僕射。

translations.literal: Sheng submitted a memorial detailing his crimes and faults; the emperor, reluctant to go against his wishes, made Yanshang Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng submitted a memorial detailing his crimes and faults. The emperor, reluctant to go against his wishes, made Yanshang Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 駱元光將殺徐庭光，謀於韓游瑰曰：「庭光辱吾祖考，吾欲殺之，馬公必怒，公能救其死乎！」

translations.literal: Luo Yuanguang was about to kill Xu Tingguang and took counsel with Han Yougui, saying: "Tingguang disgraced my forefathers; I wish to kill him. Lord Ma will surely be angry—can you save me from death?"
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yuanguang was about to kill Xu Tingguang and took counsel with Han Yougui. "Tingguang disgraced my forefathers," he said. "I want to kill him, and Lord Ma is sure to be furious. Can you save me from death?"

sentences.zh: 游瑰曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: Yougui said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: Yougui said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 壬午，遇庭光於軍門之外，揖而數其罪，命左右碎斬之。

translations.literal: On renwu, he encountered Tingguang outside the army gate, bowed and recited his crimes, and ordered those beside him to hack him to pieces and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu he encountered Tingguang outside the army gate, bowed to him, recited his crimes, and ordered his men to hack him to pieces.

sentences.zh: 入見馬燧，頓首請罪，燧大怒曰：「庭光已降，受朝廷官爵，公不告輒殺之，是無統帥也」欲斬之。

translations.literal: He entered to see Ma Sui, prostrated himself and begged pardon. Sui said in great anger: "Tingguang had already submitted and received office and rank from the court; you killed him without reporting—this is to have no commander!" He wished to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: He went in to see Ma Sui, prostrated himself, and begged pardon. Sui erupted in fury. "Tingguang had already submitted and received office and rank from the court," he said. "You killed him without reporting—this is contempt for command!" He wanted Yuanguang executed.

sentences.zh: 游瑰曰：「元光殺裨將，公猶怒如此。

translations.literal: Yougui said: "Yuanguang killed an assistant general, yet you are angry like this.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui said, "Yuanguang killed an assistant general, and you are this angry.

sentences.zh: 公殺節度使，天子其謂何！」

translations.literal: If you kill a military governor, what will the Son of Heaven say!"
translations.idiomatic: If you execute a military governor, what will the Son of Heaven say!"

sentences.zh: 燧默然。

translations.literal: Sui fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Sui fell silent.

sentences.zh: 渾瑊亦為之請，乃捨之。

translations.literal: Hun Jian also pleaded for him, and so he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian also pleaded for him, and Sui let him go.

sentences.zh: 渾瑊鎮河中，盡得李懷光之眾，朔方軍自是分居邠、蒲矣。

translations.literal: Hun Jian garrisoned Hezhong and fully received Li Huai'guang's troops; from this the Shuofang Army was divided between Bin and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian took command at Hezhong and absorbed Li Huai'guang's entire force. From then on the Shuofang Army was split between Bin and Pu.

sentences.zh: 盧龍節度使劉怦疾病，九月，己亥，詔以其子行軍司馬濟權知節度事。

translations.literal: Liu Ping, military governor of Lulong, fell ill. In the ninth month, on jihai, an edict ordered his son, Chief of Staff Ji, to serve as acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ping, military governor of Lulong, fell ill. In the ninth month, on jihai, an edict put his son Ji, chief of staff, in charge of the circuit as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 怦尋薨。

translations.literal: Ping soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Ping soon died.

sentences.zh: 己未，中書侍郎、同平章事劉從一罷為戶部尚書；

translations.literal: On jiwei, Associate Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor Liu Congyi was dismissed and made Minister of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Associate Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor Liu Congyi was dismissed and made Minister of Revenue;

sentences.zh: 庚申，薨。

translations.literal: On gengshen, he died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, he died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，上祀圜丘，赦天下。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the emperor sacrificed at the Round Altar and granted amnesty to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the emperor sacrificed at the Round Altar and granted amnesty to the realm.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲戌，戶部奏今歲入貢者凡百五十州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiaxu, the Ministry of Revenue reported that this year one hundred and fifty circuits sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiaxu, the Ministry of Revenue reported that one hundred and fifty circuits sent tribute this year.

sentences.zh: 于闐王曜上言：「兄勝讓國於臣，今請復立勝子銳。」

translations.literal: Yutian King Yao submitted a memorial: "My elder brother Sheng yielded the state to me; I now ask to reinstall Sheng's son Rui."
translations.idiomatic: Yutian King Yao submitted a memorial. "My elder brother Sheng yielded the throne to me," he wrote. "I now ask to reinstall Sheng's son Rui."

sentences.zh: 上以銳檢校光祿卿，還其國。

translations.literal: The emperor made Rui acting Director of the Imperial Household Food Service and sent him back to his state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Rui acting Director of the Imperial Household Food Service and sent him back to Yutian.

sentences.zh: 勝固辭曰：「曜久行國事，國人悅服。

translations.literal: Sheng firmly declined, saying: "Yao has long administered state affairs; the people are pleased and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng firmly declined. "Yao has long administered the kingdom's affairs," he said, "and the people are pleased and submit.

sentences.zh: 銳生長京華，不習其俗，不可往。」

translations.literal: Rui grew up in the capital; he does not know its customs and cannot go."
translations.idiomatic: Rui grew up in the capital. He does not know local customs and cannot go."

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，以銳為韶王咨議。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and made Rui Adviser to the Prince of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his response and made Rui Adviser to the Prince of Shao.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝七貞元二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong the Divine Martial Sage Literary, seventh reign year, second year of Zhenyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong of Tang, seventh reign year, second year of Zhenyuan (

sentences.zh: 丙寅，公元七八六年）

translations.literal: bingyin, 786 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingyin, AD 786)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬寅，以吏部侍郎劉滋為左散騎常侍，與給事中崔造、中書舍人齊映並同平章事。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renyin, Vice Minister of Personnel Liu Zi was made Left Regular Attendant; he, along with Supervising Secretary Cui Zao and Drafting Secretary Qi Ying, all became Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renyin, Vice Minister of Personnel Liu Zi was made Left Regular Attendant and, together with Supervising Secretary Cui Zao and Drafting Secretary Qi Ying, appointed Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 滋，子玄之孫也。

translations.literal: Zi was the grandson of Zixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zi was the grandson of Zixuan.

sentences.zh: 造少居上元，與韓會、盧東美、張正則為友，以王佐自許，時人謂之「四夔」。

translations.literal: Zao in youth lived at Shangyuan and was friends with Han Hui, Lu Dongmei, and Zhang Zhengze; he styled himself a king's assistant, and people of the time called them the "Four Kuai."
translations.idiomatic: In youth Zao lived at Shangyuan and was friends with Han Hui, Lu Dongmei, and Zhang Zhengze. He styled himself a king's assistant, and people of the time called them the "Four Kuai."

sentences.zh: 上以造在朝廷敢言，故不次用之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Zao spoke boldly at court, promoted him out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zao spoke boldly at court, the emperor promoted him out of turn.

sentences.zh: 滋、映多讓事於造。

translations.literal: Zi and Ying often deferred affairs to Zao.
translations.idiomatic: Zi and Ying often deferred affairs to Zao.

sentences.zh: 造久在江外，疾錢穀諸使罔上之弊，奏罷水陸運使、度支巡院、江、淮轉運使等，諸道租賦悉委觀察使、刺史遣官部送詣京師。

translations.literal: Zao had long been in the regions south of the Yangzi and hated the abuses of the grain-and-funds commissioners who deceived the throne; he memorialized to abolish the land-and-water transport commissioner, the revenue circuit inspection offices, the Jiang-Huai transport commissioner, and the like, and to entrust all circuit rents and levies to the observation commissioners and prefects to dispatch officials to escort them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zao had long served south of the Yangzi and hated how the grain-and-funds commissioners deceived the throne. He memorialized to abolish the land-and-water transport commissioner, the revenue circuit inspection offices, the Jiang-Huai transport commissioner, and the like, and to have every circuit's rents and levies delivered to the capital by officials dispatched by the observation commissioners and prefects.

sentences.zh: 令宰相分判尚書六曹：齊映判兵部，李勉判刑部，劉滋判吏部、禮部，造判戶部、工部，又以戶部侍郎元琇判諸道鹽鐵、榷酒，吉中孚判度支兩稅。

translations.literal: He ordered the chief ministers to divide supervision of the Six Ministries of the Department of State Affairs: Qi Ying over the Ministry of War, Li Mian over the Ministry of Justice, Liu Zi over the Ministries of Personnel and Rites, Zao over the Ministries of Revenue and Works; Yuan Xiu, Vice Minister of Revenue, was also put in charge of salt-and-iron and wine monopolies in all circuits, and Ji Zhongfu in charge of the two-tax revenue bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the chief ministers to divide supervision of the Six Ministries: Qi Ying over War, Li Mian over Justice, Liu Zi over Personnel and Rites, Zao over Revenue and Works. Yuan Xiu, Vice Minister of Revenue, was also put in charge of salt-and-iron and wine monopolies in all circuits, and Ji Zhongfu in charge of the two-tax revenue bureau.

sentences.zh: 李希烈將杜文朝寇襄州，二月，癸亥，山南東道節度使樊澤擊擒之。

translations.literal: Li Xilie's general Du Wenchao raided Xiang Prefecture. In the second month, on guihai, Fan Ze, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie's general Du Wenchao raided Xiang Prefecture. In the second month, on guihai, Fan Ze, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, attacked and captured him.

sentences.zh: 崔造與元琇善，故使判鹽鐵。

translations.literal: Cui Zao was on good terms with Yuan Xiu, so he had him supervise salt-and-iron.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zao was on good terms with Yuan Xiu, so he put him in charge of salt-and-iron.

sentences.zh: 韓滉奏論鹽鐵過失；

translations.literal: Han Huang submitted a memorial discussing faults in salt-and-iron administration;
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang submitted a memorial discussing faults in salt-and-iron administration;

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以琇為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Xiu was made Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Xiu was made Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 陝州水陸運使李泌奏：「自集津至三門，鑿山開車道十八里，以避底柱之險。」

translations.literal: Li Bi, land-and-water transport commissioner of Shan Prefecture, submitted a memorial: "From Jijin to Sanmen, we carved through the mountains and opened an eighteen-li cart road to avoid the peril of Dizhu."
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi, land-and-water transport commissioner of Shan Prefecture, submitted a memorial. "From Jijin to Sanmen," he wrote, "we carved through the mountains and opened an eighteen-li cart road to avoid the peril of Dizhu."

sentences.zh: 是月道成。

translations.literal: That month the road was completed.
translations.idiomatic: That month the road was completed.

sentences.zh: 三月，李希烈別將寇鄭州，義成節度使李澄擊破之。

translations.literal: In the third month, one of Li Xilie's other generals raided Zheng Prefecture; Li Cheng, military governor of Yicheng, attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, one of Li Xilie's other generals raided Zheng Prefecture. Li Cheng, military governor of Yicheng, attacked and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 希烈兵勢日蹙，會有疾。

translations.literal: Xilie's military strength grew tighter day by day, and then he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie's military position grew tighter day by day, and then he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙寅，大將陳仙奇使醫陳山甫毒殺之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingyin, the great general Chen Xianqi had the physician Chen Shanfu poison and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on bingyin, the great general Chen Xianqi had the physician Chen Shanfu poison and kill him.

sentences.zh: 因以兵悉誅其兄弟妻子，舉眾來降。

translations.literal: He then used troops to execute all of Xilie's brothers, wives, and children, and came in surrender with the whole host.
translations.idiomatic: He then had troops execute all of Xilie's brothers, wives, and children and came in surrender with the whole host.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以仙奇為淮西節度使。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Xianqi was made military governor of Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Xianqi was made military governor of Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 關中倉廩竭，禁軍或自脫巾呼於道曰：「拘吾於軍而不給糧，吾罪人也！」

translations.literal: The granaries of Guanzhong were exhausted; some of the imperial guard stripped off their headcloths and cried in the roads, saying: "You keep us bound in the army and give us no grain—we are treated like criminals!"
translations.idiomatic: The granaries of Guanzhong were exhausted. Some of the imperial guard stripped off their headcloths and cried in the streets, "You keep us bound in the army and give us no grain—we are treated like criminals!"

sentences.zh: 上憂之甚，會韓滉運米三萬斛至陝，李泌即奏之。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply worried; just then Han Huang transported thirty thousand hu of grain to Shan, and Li Bi immediately reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply worried. Just then Han Huang transported thirty thousand hu of grain to Shan, and Li Bi immediately reported it.

sentences.zh: 上喜，遽至東宮，謂太子曰：「米已至陝，吾父子得生矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor rejoiced, hurried to the Eastern Palace, and said to the crown prince: "The grain has reached Shan—father and son can live!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejoiced, hurried to the Eastern Palace, and told the crown prince, "The grain has reached Shan—father and son can live!"

sentences.zh: 時禁中不釀，命於坊市取酒為樂。

translations.literal: At that time brewing was forbidden in the palace precincts; he ordered wine fetched from the wards and markets for celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Brewing was forbidden in the palace precincts at the time, so he ordered wine fetched from the wards and markets for celebration.

sentences.zh: 又遣中使諭神策六軍，軍士皆呼萬歲。

translations.literal: He also sent palace envoys to announce it to the six Shence armies, and the soldiers all shouted "Long live [the emperor]!"
translations.idiomatic: He also sent palace envoys to announce it to the six Shence armies, and the soldiers all shouted "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 時比歲饑饉，兵民率皆瘦黑，至是麥始熟，市有醉人，當時以為嘉瑞。

translations.literal: For years there had been famine; soldiers and common people were mostly thin and dark-skinned. Now the wheat had just ripened, and there were drunk men in the markets—people at the time took this as an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: For years there had been famine, and soldiers and common people were mostly thin and dark-skinned. Now the wheat had just ripened, and there were drunk men in the markets—people at the time took this as an auspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 人乍飽食，死者復伍之一。

translations.literal: When people suddenly ate their fill, one in five died.
translations.idiomatic: When people suddenly ate their fill again, one in five died.

sentences.zh: 數月，有膚色乃復故。

translations.literal: After several months those who survived saw their skin color return to normal.
translations.idiomatic: After several months those who survived saw their skin color return to normal.

sentences.zh: 以橫海軍使程日華為節度使。

translations.literal: Cheng Rihua, commissioner of the Henghai Army, was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Rihua, commissioner of the Henghai Army, was made military governor.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，淮西兵馬使吳少誠殺陳仙奇，自為留後。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Wu Shaoqian, Huai West army-and-horse commissioner, killed Chen Xianqi and made himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Wu Shaoqian, Huai West army-and-horse commissioner, killed Chen Xianqi and made himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 少誠素狡險，為李希烈所寵任，故為之報仇。

translations.literal: Shaoqian was by nature crafty and treacherous and had been favored and trusted by Li Xilie, so he avenged him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqian was by nature crafty and treacherous and had been favored and trusted by Li Xilie, so he avenged him.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以虔王諒為申、光、隨、蔡節度大使，以少誠為留後。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Prince of Qian Liang was made grand commissioner of the Shen-Guang-Sui-Cai circuit, and Shaoqian was made acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Prince of Qian Liang was made grand commissioner of the Shen-Guang-Sui-Cai circuit, and Shaoqian was made acting governor.

sentences.zh: 以隴右行營節度使曲環為陳許節度使。

translations.literal: Qu Huan, military governor of the Longyou field headquarters, was made military governor of Chenxu.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Huan, military governor of the Longyou field headquarters, was made military governor of Chenxu.

sentences.zh: 陳許荒亂之餘，戶口流散。

translations.literal: After the desolation and disorder of Chenxu, households and population had scattered.
translations.idiomatic: After the desolation and disorder of Chenxu, households and population had scattered.

sentences.zh: 曲環以勤儉率下，政令寬簡，賦役平均，數年之間，流亡復業，兵食皆足。

translations.literal: Qu Huan led his subordinates in diligence and frugality; government orders were broad and simple, and levies and corvée were even. Within a few years the displaced returned to their occupations, and both troops and provisions were sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Huan led his subordinates in diligence and frugality. Government orders were broad and simple, and levies and corvée were even. Within a few years the displaced returned to their occupations, and both troops and provisions were sufficient.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸未，義成節度使李澄薨，其子克寧謀總軍務，秘不發喪。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on guiwei, Li Cheng, military governor of Yicheng, died. His son Ke'ning plotted to take overall command of military affairs and secretly did not announce the death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guiwei, Li Cheng, military governor of Yicheng, died. His son Ke'ning plotted to take overall command of military affairs and secretly withheld news of the death.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，吐蕃尚結贊大舉寇涇、隴、邠、寧，掠人畜，芟禾稼，西鄙騷然，州縣各城守，詔渾將萬人，駱元光將八千人屯咸陽以備之。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Shang Jiezan of Tibet launched a great raid against Jing, Long, Bin, and Ning, plundering people and livestock and cutting down grain crops. The western frontier was in uproar; prefectures and counties each walled themselves for defense. An edict ordered Hun Jian to lead ten thousand men and Luo Yuanguang eight thousand to encamp at Xianyang in preparation.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Shang Jiezan of Tibet launched a great raid against Jing, Long, Bin, and Ning, plundering people and livestock and cutting down grain crops. The western frontier was in uproar, and prefectures and counties each walled themselves for defense. An edict ordered Hun Jian to lead ten thousand men and Luo Yuanguang eight thousand to encamp at Xianyang in preparation.

sentences.zh: 初，上與常侍李泌議復府兵，泌因為上歷敘府兵自西魏以來興廢之由，且言：「府兵平日皆安居田畝，每府有折衝領之，折衝以農隙教習戰陳。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor discussed restoring the militia system with Regular Attendant Li Bi. Bi thereupon for the emperor narrated in sequence the reasons for the rise and fall of the militia from the Western Wei onward, and said: "In ordinary times militia soldiers all lived peacefully on their fields; each militia district had a frontier-stand commander to lead them, and in the gaps between farm work the commander taught battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor discussed restoring the militia system with Regular Attendant Li Bi. Bi then narrated for him the reasons for the rise and fall of the militia from the Western Wei onward and said, "In ordinary times militia soldiers all lived peacefully on their fields. Each militia district had a frontier-stand commander to lead them, and in the gaps between farm work the commander taught battle formations.

sentences.zh: 國家有事征發，則以符契下其州及府，參驗發之，至所期處。

translations.literal: When the state had business and mobilized troops, tally-documents were sent down to the prefecture and militia district, verified, and the men were dispatched to arrive at the appointed place.
translations.idiomatic: When the state mobilized, tally-documents were sent down to the prefecture and militia district, verified, and the men were dispatched to arrive at the appointed place.

sentences.zh: 將帥按閱，有教習不精者，罪其折衝，甚者罪及刺史。

translations.literal: The commanding general inspected them; if training was not thorough, the frontier-stand commander was punished, and in serious cases the punishment reached the prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The commanding general inspected them. If training was not thorough, the frontier-stand commander was punished, and in serious cases the punishment reached the prefect.

sentences.zh: 軍還，則賜勳加賞，便道罷之。

translations.literal: When the army returned, merit was granted and rewards added, and they were dismissed by the nearest route.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, merit was granted and rewards added, and they were dismissed by the nearest route.

sentences.zh: 行者近不逾時，遠不經歲。

translations.literal: Those who went out on campaign, if near, did not exceed the season; if far, did not pass a year.
translations.idiomatic: Those who went out on campaign, if near, did not exceed the season; if far, did not pass a year.

sentences.zh: 高宗以劉仁軌為洮河鎮守使以圖吐蕃，於是始有久戍之役。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong made Liu Ren'gui frontier commander of the Tao River to scheme against Tibet, and from this there first arose long-term garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong made Liu Ren'gui frontier commander of the Tao River to scheme against Tibet, and from this there first arose long-term garrison service.

sentences.zh: 武後以來，承平日久，府兵浸墮，為人所賤，百姓恥之，至蒸熨手足以避其役。

translations.literal: From Empress Wu onward, peace lasted long and the militia gradually decayed; men were despised for it, common people were ashamed of it, and some even steamed and pressed their hands and feet to evade the service.
translations.idiomatic: From Empress Wu onward, peace lasted long and the militia gradually decayed. Men were despised for it, common people were ashamed of it, and some even steamed and pressed their hands and feet to evade the service.

sentences.zh: 又，牛仙客以積財得宰相，邊將效之。

translations.literal: Moreover, Niu Xianke became chief minister through amassed wealth, and frontier generals imitated him.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Niu Xianke became chief minister through amassed wealth, and frontier generals imitated him.

sentences.zh: 山東戍卒多繼繒帛自隨，邊將誘之寄於府庫，晝則若役，夜縶地牢，利其死而沒入其財。

translations.literal: Shandong garrison soldiers often carried silk goods with them in succession; frontier generals enticed them to deposit them in the treasury stores, by day treated them like corvée labor, and by night bound them in underground cells, profiting from their deaths to confiscate their property.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong garrison soldiers often carried silk goods with them. Frontier generals enticed them to deposit the goods in treasury stores, by day treated them like corvée labor, and by night bound them in underground cells, profiting from their deaths to confiscate their property.

sentences.zh: 故自天寶以後，山東戍卒還者什無二三，其殘虐如此。

translations.literal: Therefore from after the Tianbao era, of Shandong garrison soldiers who returned, not two or three in ten survived—such was the cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore from after the Tianbao era, of Shandong garrison soldiers who returned, not two or three in ten survived—such was the cruelty.

sentences.zh: 然未嘗有外叛內侮，殺帥自擅者，誠以顧戀田園，恐累宗族故也。

translations.literal: Yet there were never cases of outward rebellion or inward insolence, of killing commanders and seizing power for themselves—truly because they cherished their fields and gardens and feared harm to their clans.
translations.idiomatic: Yet there were never cases of outward rebellion or inward insolence, of killing commanders and seizing power for themselves—truly because they cherished their fields and gardens and feared harm to their clans.

sentences.zh: 自開元之末，張說始募長徵兵，謂之弓廣騎，其後益為六軍。

translations.literal: From the end of the Kaiyuan era, Zhang Yue first recruited long-service soldiers, calling them expanded cavalry (kuo cavalry); afterward they were further expanded into the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: From the end of the Kaiyuan era, Zhang Yue first recruited long-service soldiers, calling them expanded cavalry (kuo cavalry). They were later expanded further into the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 及李林甫為相，奏諸軍皆募人為之。

translations.literal: When Li Linfu became chief minister, he memorialized that all armies should recruit men for service.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Linfu became chief minister, he memorialized that all armies should recruit men for service.

sentences.zh: 兵不土著，又無宗族，不自重惜，忘身徇利，禍亂遂生，至今為梗。

translations.literal: The soldiers were not rooted to the soil and had no clans; they did not value themselves, forgot their persons and pursued profit, and disaster and disorder arose—down to the present they remain an obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were not rooted to the soil and had no clans. They did not value themselves, forgot their persons and pursued profit, and disaster and disorder arose—down to the present they remain an obstruction.

sentences.zh: 曏使府兵之法常存不廢，安有如此下陵上替之患哉！

translations.literal: If only the militia law had always remained and not been abolished, how could there be such a calamity of subordinates overbearing and superiors displaced!
translations.idiomatic: If only the militia law had always remained and not been abolished, how could there be such a calamity of subordinates overbearing and superiors displaced!

sentences.zh: 陛下思復府兵，此乃社稷之福，太平有日矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty thinks to restore the militia—this is the fortune of the altars of soil and grain; peace will come in its day."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty thinks to restore the militia—this is the fortune of the altars of soil and grain; peace will come in its day."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「俟平河中，當與卿議之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wait until Hezhong is pacified; then I shall discuss it with you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wait until Hezhong is pacified; then I shall discuss it with you."

sentences.zh: 九月，丁亥，詔十六衛各置上將軍，以寵功臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dinghai, an edict ordered each of the Sixteen Guards to appoint a senior general, to honor meritorious officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dinghai, an edict ordered each of the Sixteen Guards to appoint a senior general, to honor meritorious officials.

sentences.zh: 改神策左、右廂為左、右神策軍，殿前射生左、右廂為殿前左、右射生軍，各置大將軍二人、將軍二人。

translations.literal: The left and right wings of the Shence Army were changed to the Left and Right Shence Armies; the left and right wings of the Palace Front Archery Guard were changed to the Left and Right Palace Front Archery Armies; each was given two great generals and two generals.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right wings of the Shence Army were changed to the Left and Right Shence Armies. The left and right wings of the Palace Front Archery Guard were changed to the Left and Right Palace Front Archery Armies. Each was given two great generals and two generals.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，李克寧始發父澄之喪，殺行軍司馬馬鉉，墨縗出視事，增兵城門。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Li Ke'ning at last announced his father Cheng's death, killed Chief of Staff Ma Xuan, came out in unbleached mourning garb to conduct affairs, and increased troops at the city gates.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Li Ke'ning at last announced his father Cheng's death, killed Chief of Staff Ma Xuan, came out in unbleached mourning garb to conduct affairs, and increased troops at the city gates.

sentences.zh: 劉玄佐出師屯境上以制之，且使告諭切至，克寧乃不敢襲位。

translations.literal: Liu Xuanzuo marched out and encamped on the border to restrain him, and also sent envoys with urgent admonition; Ke'ning then did not dare seize the post.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanzuo marched out and encamped on the border to restrain him and also sent envoys with urgent admonition. Ke'ning then did not dare seize the post.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以東都留守賈耽為義成節度使，。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Eastern Capital Regent Jia Dan was made military governor of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Eastern Capital Regent Jia Dan was made military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 克寧悉取府庫之財夜出，軍士從而剽之，比明殆盡。

translations.literal: Ke'ning took all the wealth of the treasury stores out by night; soldiers followed and plundered it, and by dawn it was nearly gone.
translations.idiomatic: Ke'ning took all the wealth of the treasury stores out by night. Soldiers followed and plundered it, and by dawn it was nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 淄青兵數千自行營歸，過滑州，將佐皆曰：「李納雖外奉朝命，內畜兼併之志，請館其兵於城外。」

translations.literal: Several thousand Ziqing troops were returning from their own encampment and passed through Hua Prefecture. The officers all said: "Although Li Na outwardly follows the court's orders, inwardly he harbors designs of annexation—please quarter his troops outside the city."
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand Ziqing troops were returning from their own encampment and passed through Hua Prefecture. The officers all said, "Although Li Na outwardly follows the court's orders, inwardly he harbors designs of annexation. Please quarter his troops outside the city."

sentences.zh: 賈耽曰：「奈何與人鄰道而野處其將士乎！」

translations.literal: Jia Dan said: "How can we have a neighboring road and leave their officers and soldiers to camp in the open!"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan said, "How can we share a neighboring road and leave their officers and soldiers to camp in the open!"

sentences.zh: 命館於城中。

translations.literal: He ordered them quartered inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them quartered inside the city.

sentences.zh: 耽時引百騎獵於納境，納聞之，大喜，服其度量，不敢犯也。

translations.literal: Dan at times led a hundred horsemen to hunt in Na's territory; Na heard of it, rejoiced greatly, admired his magnanimity, and did not dare encroach.
translations.idiomatic: Dan at times led a hundred horsemen to hunt in Na's territory. Na heard of it, rejoiced greatly, admired his magnanimity, and did not dare encroach.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃游騎及好畤。

translations.literal: Tibetan raiding cavalry reached Haozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan raiding cavalry reached Haozhi.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，京城戒嚴，復遣左金吾將軍張獻甫屯咸陽。

translations.literal: On yisi, the capital was placed under martial law, and Left Golden Guard General Zhang Xianfu was again sent to encamp at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, the capital was placed under martial law, and Left Golden Guard General Zhang Xianfu was again sent to encamp at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 民間傳言復欲出幸以避吐蕃，齊映見上言曰：「外間皆言陛下已理裝，具糗糧，人情心兇懼。

translations.literal: Among the people rumor spread that the emperor again intended to go on tour to escape the Tibetans. Qi Ying saw the emperor and said: "Outside everyone says Your Majesty has already packed baggage and prepared dry rations; hearts among the people are fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Among the people rumor spread that the emperor again intended to go on tour to escape the Tibetans. Qi Ying saw the emperor and said, "Outside everyone says you have already packed baggage and prepared dry rations. Hearts among the people are fearful and alarmed.

sentences.zh: 夫大福不再，陛下奈何不與臣等熟計之！」

translations.literal: Great fortune does not come twice—Your Majesty, why not discuss this thoroughly with your ministers!"
translations.idiomatic: Great fortune does not come twice—why not discuss this thoroughly with your ministers!"

sentences.zh: 因伏地流涕，上亦為之動容。

translations.literal: He then prostrated himself and wept; the emperor too was moved in countenance.
translations.idiomatic: He then prostrated himself and wept, and the emperor too was moved.

sentences.zh: 李晟遣其將王佖將驍勇三千伏於汧城，戒之曰：「虜過城下，勿擊其首；

translations.literal: Li Sheng sent his general Wang Bi with three thousand fierce warriors to lie in ambush at Qian City and warned him, saying: "When the barbarians pass below the city, do not strike their vanguard;
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng sent his general Wang Bi with three thousand fierce warriors to lie in ambush at Qian City and warned him, "When the barbarians pass below the city, do not strike their vanguard.

sentences.zh: 首雖敗，彼全軍而至，汝弗能當也。

translations.literal: though the vanguard is defeated, their whole army will arrive and you will not be able to withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the vanguard is defeated, their whole army will arrive and you will not be able to withstand them.

sentences.zh: 不若俟前軍已過，見五方旗，虎豹衣，乃其中軍也，出其不意擊之，必大捷。」

translations.literal: Better to wait until the forward army has passed, and when you see the five-direction banners and tiger-and-leopard garb—that is their center army—strike them by surprise; you will surely win a great victory."
translations.idiomatic: Better to wait until the forward army has passed. When you see the five-direction banners and tiger-and-leopard garb—that is their center army—strike them by surprise and you will surely win a great victory."

sentences.zh: 佖用其言，尚結贊敗走。

translations.literal: Bi followed his advice, and Shang Jiezan was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Bi followed his advice, and Shang Jiezan was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 軍士不識尚結贊，僅而獲免。

translations.literal: The soldiers did not recognize Shang Jiezan, and he barely escaped capture.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers did not recognize Shang Jiezan, and he barely escaped capture.

sentences.zh: 尚結贊謂其徒曰：「唐之良將，李晟、馬燧、渾瑊而已，當以計去之。」

translations.literal: Shang Jiezan said to his followers: "Tang's good generals are only Li Sheng, Ma Sui, and Hun Jian; we should use stratagem to remove them."
translations.idiomatic: Shang Jiezan said to his followers, "Tang's good generals are only Li Sheng, Ma Sui, and Hun Jian. We should use stratagem to remove them."

sentences.zh: 入鳳翔境內，無所俘掠，以兵二萬直抵城下曰：「李令公召我來，何不出犒我！」

translations.literal: Entering Fengxiang territory, he plundered nothing; with twenty thousand troops he went straight to the foot of the wall and said: "Marshal Li summoned me here—why do you not come out and reward my troops!"
translations.idiomatic: Entering Fengxiang territory, he plundered nothing. With twenty thousand troops he went straight to the foot of the wall and said, "Marshal Li summoned me here—why do you not come out and reward my troops!"

sentences.zh: 經宿，乃引退。

translations.literal: After one night he then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After one night he then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸亥，李晟遣蕃落使野詩良輔與王佖將步騎五千襲吐蕃摧砂堡。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on guihai, Li Sheng sent Tribal Affairs Commissioner Ye Shiliangfu and Wang Bi to lead five thousand infantry and cavalry in a raid on the Tibetan fortress of Cuisha.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on guihai, Li Sheng sent Tribal Affairs Commissioner Ye Shiliangfu and Wang Bi to lead five thousand infantry and cavalry in a raid on the Tibetan fortress of Cuisha.

sentences.zh: 壬申，遇吐蕃眾二萬，與戰，破之，乘勝逐北，至堡下，攻拔之，斬其將扈屈律悉蒙，焚其蓄積而還。

translations.literal: On renshen, they encountered twenty thousand Tibetans, fought them, defeated them, pursued the fleeing enemy in victory to the foot of the fortress, stormed and took it, beheaded the general Hu Qulü Ximeng, burned its stores, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, they encountered twenty thousand Tibetans, fought them, and defeated them. Pursuing the fleeing enemy in victory to the foot of the fortress, they stormed and took it, beheaded the general Hu Qulü Ximeng, burned its stores, and returned.

sentences.zh: 尚結贊引兵自寧、慶北去，癸酉，軍於合水之北。

translations.literal: Shang Jiezan led troops north from Ning and Qing; on guiyou, he encamped north of Heshui.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Jiezan led his army north from Ning and Qing. On the day guiyou, he encamped north of Heshui.

sentences.zh: 邠寧節度使韓游瑰遣其將史履程夜襲其營，殺數百人。

translations.literal: Binning Jiedushi Han Yougui sent his general Shi Lücheng to raid their camp by night, killing several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui, military governor of Binning, sent his general Shi Lücheng to raid the enemy camp by night and killed several hundred men.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃追之，游瑰陳於平川，潛使人鼓於西山。

translations.literal: The Tibetans pursued. Yougui drew up battle lines on open ground and secretly sent men to beat drums on the western hills.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans gave chase. Yougui formed his line on open ground and secretly had men beat drums on the western hills.

sentences.zh: 虜驚，棄所掠而去。

translations.literal: The barbarians were alarmed, abandoned what they had plundered, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy panicked, dropped their loot, and fled.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲午，立淑妃王氏為皇后。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiawu, the Elegant Consort Lady Wang was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day jiawu, the Elegant Consort Lady Wang was elevated to empress.

sentences.zh: 乙未，韓滉入朝。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Han Huang entered the capital for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Han Huang came to court.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，皇后崩。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the empress died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, the empress died.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，吐蕃寇鹽州，謂刺史杜彥光曰：「我欲得城，聽爾率人去。」

translations.literal: On xinchou, the Tibetans attacked Yan Prefecture and said to Prefect Du Yanguang: "I want the city—take your people and go."
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the Tibetans attacked Yan Prefecture and said to Prefect Du Yanguang, "I want the city. Take your people and go."

sentences.zh: 彥光悉眾奔鄜州，吐蕃入據之。

translations.literal: Du Yanguang led all his people in flight to Bin Prefecture, and the Tibetans entered and occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yanguang led all his people in flight to Bin Prefecture, and the Tibetans entered and took the city.

sentences.zh: 劉玄佐在汴，習鄰道故事，久未入朝。

translations.literal: Liu Xuanzuo was at Bian and, following the old practice of neighboring circuits, had long failed to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanzuo was stationed at Bian. Following the old custom of neighboring circuits, he had long stayed away from court.

sentences.zh: 韓滉過汴，玄佐重其才望，以屬吏禮謁之。

translations.literal: When Han Huang passed through Bian, Xuanzuo, respecting his talent and reputation, received him with the ceremony due a subordinate official.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Huang passed through Bian, Xuanzuo, impressed by his talent and standing, received him with the ceremony owed a subordinate officer.

sentences.zh: 滉相約為兄弟，請拜玄佐母。

translations.literal: Huang proposed that they become sworn brothers and asked to pay respects to Xuanzuo's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Huang proposed they become sworn brothers and asked to pay his respects to Xuanzuo's mother.

sentences.zh: 其母喜，置酒見之。

translations.literal: His mother was pleased and set out wine to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was delighted and set out wine to receive him.

sentences.zh: 酒半，滉曰：「弟何時入朝？」

translations.literal: When the wine was halfway through, Huang said: "Brother, when will you come to court?"
translations.idiomatic: When they were halfway through the wine, Huang said, "Brother, when do you plan to come to court?"

sentences.zh: 玄佐曰：「久欲入朝，但力未辦耳。」

translations.literal: Xuanzuo said: "I have long wished to come to court, but have not had the means."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzuo said, "I have long wanted to come to court, but I have not had the means to do it."

sentences.zh: 滉曰：「滉力可及，弟宜早入朝。

translations.literal: Huang said: "Huang can help with that—brother, you ought to come to court soon.
translations.idiomatic: Huang said, "I can help with that. Brother, you ought to come to court soon.

sentences.zh: 丈母垂白，不可使更帥諸婦女往填宮也！」

translations.literal: Your mother-in-law's hair is already white—you cannot let her lead the other women to the palace again!"
translations.idiomatic: Your mother-in-law's hair is already white. You cannot make her lead the other women to court again!"

sentences.zh: 母悲泣不自勝。

translations.literal: The mother wept in grief beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: The mother wept until she could no longer bear it.

sentences.zh: 滉乃遺玄佐錢二十萬緡，備行裝。

translations.literal: Huang then gave Xuanzuo two hundred thousand strings of cash for travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Huang then gave Xuanzuo two hundred thousand strings of cash to cover his travel expenses.

sentences.zh: 滉留大梁三日，大出金帛賞勞，一軍為之傾動。

translations.literal: Huang stayed three days at Daliang and lavished gold and silk in rewards; the whole army was stirred by it.
translations.idiomatic: Huang remained at Daliang for three days and distributed gold and silk in lavish rewards, stirring the entire army.

sentences.zh: 玄佐驚服，既而遣人密聽之，滉問孔目吏，「今日所費幾何？」

translations.literal: Xuanzuo was astonished and impressed; then he secretly sent someone to listen in—Huang was questioning the ledger clerk, "How much was spent today?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzuo was astonished and impressed. Then he secretly sent someone to eavesdrop. Huang was questioning the ledger clerk: "How much was spent today?"

sentences.zh: 詰責甚細。

translations.literal: He pressed the accounting in minute detail.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the accounting in minute detail.

sentences.zh: 玄佐笑曰：「吾知之矣！」

translations.literal: Xuanzuo laughed and said: "Now I understand!"
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzuo laughed and said, "Now I understand!"

sentences.zh: 壬寅，玄佐與陳許節度使曲環俱入朝。

translations.literal: On renyin, Xuanzuo and Chenxu Jiedushi Qu Huan both entered the capital for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Xuanzuo and Chenxu military governor Qu Huan both came to court.

sentences.zh: 崔造改錢穀法，事多不集。

translations.literal: Cui Zao reformed the fiscal and grain laws, but many of his measures failed to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zao reformed the fiscal and grain laws, but many of his plans never took hold.

sentences.zh: 諸使之職，行之已久，中外安之。

translations.literal: The commissioner posts had been in place a long time, and court and provinces alike had grown accustomed to them.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner posts had long been in place, and both court and provinces had grown used to them.

sentences.zh: 元琇既失職，造憂懼成疾，不視事。

translations.literal: After Yuan Heng lost his position, Zao grew ill with worry and fear and ceased handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Heng lost his post, Zao fell ill with worry and fear and stopped attending to business.

sentences.zh: 既而江、淮運米大至，上嘉韓滉之功。

translations.literal: Before long, transport grain from the Jiang and Huai regions arrived in great quantity, and the emperor praised Han Huang's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, transport grain from the Jiang and Huai regions arrived in great quantity, and the emperor praised Han Huang's achievement.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁巳，以滉兼度支、諸道鹽鐵，轉運等使，造所條奏皆改之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dingsi, Huang was additionally appointed Commissioner of Revenue, Salt and Iron for All Circuits, and Transport; every proposal Zao had submitted was overturned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingsi, Huang was made commissioner of revenue, salt and iron for all circuits, and transport as well. Every proposal Zao had submitted was reversed.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃又寇夏州，亦令刺史托跋乾暉帥眾去，遂據其城。

translations.literal: The Tibetans again attacked Xia Prefecture and likewise ordered Prefect Toba Qianhui to lead his people away, then seized the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans attacked Xia Prefecture again, likewise ordering Prefect Toba Qianhui to lead his people away, then seized the city.

sentences.zh: 又寇銀州，州素無城，吏民皆潰。

translations.literal: They also attacked Yin Prefecture; the prefecture had never had walls, and officials and commoners all fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: They also attacked Yin Prefecture. The prefecture had never had walls, and officials and commoners alike fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃亦棄之，又陷麟州。

translations.literal: The Tibetans abandoned it as well and then took Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans abandoned Yin as well and then captured Lin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 韓滉屢短元琇於上。

translations.literal: Han Huang repeatedly spoke against Yuan Heng before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang repeatedly slandered Yuan Heng before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 庚申，崔造罷為右庶子，琇貶雷州司戶。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Cui Zao was removed and made Right Household Companion; Heng was demoted to Registrar of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Cui Zao was dismissed and made Right Household Companion; Heng was demoted to registrar of Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 以吏部侍郎班宏為戶部侍郎、度支副使。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Ban Hong was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and deputy commissioner of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Hong, vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was appointed vice minister of revenue and deputy commissioner of revenue.

sentences.zh: 韓游瑰奏請發兵攻鹽州，吐蕃救之，則使河東襲其背。

translations.literal: Han Yougui memorialized requesting troops to attack Yan Prefecture; if the Tibetans came to its rescue, Hedong forces should strike their rear.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui memorialized asking that troops be sent to attack Yan Prefecture. If the Tibetans came to its rescue, Hedong forces should strike them from behind.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，詔駱元光及陳許兵馬使韓全義將步騎萬二千人會邠寧軍，趣鹽州，又使馬燧以河東軍擊吐蕃。

translations.literal: On bingyin, an edict ordered Luo Yuanguang and Chenxu military commissioner Han Quanyi to lead twelve thousand infantry and cavalry to join the Binning army and march on Yan Prefecture, and also ordered Ma Sui to strike the Tibetans with the Hedong army.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, an edict ordered Luo Yuanguang and Chenxu military commissioner Han Quanyi to lead twelve thousand infantry and cavalry to join the Binning army and march on Yan Prefecture. Ma Sui was also ordered to strike the Tibetans with the Hedong army.

sentences.zh: 燧至右州，河曲六胡州皆降，遷於雲、朔之間。

translations.literal: Sui reached Youzhou; the six Hu prefectures in the river bend all surrendered and were relocated between Yun and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Sui reached You Prefecture. The six Hu prefectures in the river bend all surrendered and were relocated between Yun and Shuo.

sentences.zh: 工部侍郎張彧，李晟之婿也。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works Zhang Yu was Li Sheng's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu, vice minister of the Ministry of Works, was Li Sheng's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 晟在鳳翔，以女嫁慕客崔樞，禮重樞過於彧。

translations.literal: When Sheng was at Fengxiang, he married his daughter to guest-official Cui Shu and treated Shu with greater courtesy than Yu.
translations.idiomatic: While Sheng was at Fengxiang, he married his daughter to the guest-official Cui Shu and treated Shu with greater honor than Yu.

sentences.zh: 彧怒，遂附於張延賞；

translations.literal: Yu was enraged and attached himself to Zhang Yanshang;
translations.idiomatic: Yu was enraged and threw in his lot with Zhang Yanshang;

sentences.zh: 給事中鄭雲逵嘗為晟行軍司馬，失晟意，亦附延賞。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zheng Yunkui had once served Sheng as army camp adjutant but lost Sheng's favor and also attached himself to Yanshang.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zheng Yunkui had once served as Sheng's army camp adjutant but lost Sheng's favor and also joined Yanshang.

sentences.zh: 上亦忌晟功名。
