translations.literal: The emperor also grew wary of Sheng's merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also grew wary of Sheng's achievements and renown.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃有離間之言，延賞等騰謗於朝，無所不至。

translations.literal: Just then the Tibetans circulated words of discord, and Yanshang and others spread slanders at court without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Tibetans spread words meant to sow discord, and Yanshang and others broadcast slanders at court without restraint.

sentences.zh: 晟聞之，晝夜泣，目為之腫，悉遣子弟詣長安，表請削髮為僧，上慰諭，不許。

translations.literal: Sheng heard of it and wept day and night until his eyes swelled; he sent all his sons and younger brothers to Chang'an with a memorial asking to shave his head and become a monk. The emperor comforted and admonished him and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng heard of it, he wept day and night until his eyes swelled. He sent all his sons and younger brothers to Chang'an with a memorial asking to shave his head and become a monk. The emperor comforted him and refused.

sentences.zh: 辛未，於朝，見上，自陳足疾，懇辭方鎮，上不許。

translations.literal: On xinwei, at court, he saw the emperor, declared himself afflicted with foot ailment, and earnestly begged to resign his regional command—the emperor would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, at court, he saw the emperor, pleaded foot ailment, and earnestly asked to be relieved of his regional command. The emperor would not agree.

sentences.zh: 韓滉素與晟善，上命滉與劉玄佐諭旨於晟，使與延賞釋怨。

translations.literal: Han Huang had long been on good terms with Sheng; the emperor ordered Huang and Liu Xuanzuo to convey the imperial will to Sheng and have him reconcile with Yanshang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang had long been on good terms with Sheng. The emperor ordered Huang and Liu Xuanzuo to convey the imperial will to Sheng and have him reconcile with Yanshang.

sentences.zh: 晟奉詔，滉等引延賞詣晟第謝，結為兄弟，因宴飲盡歡。

translations.literal: Sheng obeyed the edict; Huang and the others brought Yanshang to Sheng's residence to apologize; they became sworn brothers and feasted together in full conviviality.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng obeyed the edict. Huang and the others brought Yanshang to Sheng's residence to apologize. They became sworn brothers and feasted together in full good cheer.

sentences.zh: 又宴於滉、玄佐之第，亦如之。

translations.literal: They feasted again at the residences of Huang and Xuanzuo in the same manner.
translations.idiomatic: They held feasts again at the residences of Huang and Xuanzuo in the same manner.

sentences.zh: 滉因使晟表薦延賞為相。

translations.literal: Huang then had Sheng submit a memorial recommending Yanshang as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Huang then had Sheng submit a memorial recommending Yanshang for the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝七貞元三年（

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong the Divine Martial Sage Literary, seventh year, third year of Zhenyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong the Divine Martial Sage Literary, seventh reign year, third year of Zhenyuan (

sentences.zh: 丁卯，公元七八七年）

translations.literal: dingmao, AD 787)
translations.idiomatic: dingmao, AD 787)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬寅，以左僕射張延賞同平章事。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renyin, Left Pushe Zhang Yanshang was made co-chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renyin, Left Pushe Zhang Yanshang was appointed co-chief minister.

sentences.zh: 李晟為其子請婚於延賞，延賞不許。

translations.literal: Li Sheng asked Yanshang for his son's marriage; Yanshang refused.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng asked Yanshang to marry his son to Yanshang's daughter. Yanshang refused.

sentences.zh: 晟謂人曰：「武夫性快，釋也於杯酒間，則不復貯胸中矣。

translations.literal: Sheng said to others: "A fighting man is quick-tempered—once anger is released over wine, it is not stored in the breast again.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said to others, "A fighting man is quick-tempered. Once anger is released over wine, it is not stored in the breast again.

sentences.zh: 非如文士難犯，外雖和解，內蓄憾如故，吾得無懼哉！」

translations.literal: Not like literary men whom one must not offend—outwardly reconciled, inwardly resentful as before—how can I not fear!"
translations.idiomatic: Literary men are not like that—they are hard to offend. Outwardly reconciled, inwardly resentful as before—how can I not fear!"

sentences.zh: 初，李希烈據淮西，選騎兵尤精者為左、右門槍、奉國四將，步兵尤精者為左、右克平十將。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Li Xilie held Huai West, he selected the finest cavalry as the four Left and Right Gate-Spear and Serving-the-State commanders, and the finest infantry as the ten Left and Right Ke-ping commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Li Xilie held Huai West, he selected the finest cavalry for the four Left and Right Gate-Spear and Serving-the-State commands, and the finest infantry for the ten Left and Right Ke-ping commands.

sentences.zh: 淮西少馬，精兵皆乘騾，謂之騾軍。

translations.literal: Huai West had few horses; elite troops all rode mules—they were called the Mule Army.
translations.idiomatic: Huai West had few horses, so elite troops all rode mules. They were called the Mule Army.

sentences.zh: 陳仙奇舉淮西降，才數月，詔發其兵於京西防秋。

translations.literal: Chen Xianqi had surrendered Huai West only a few months earlier when an edict ordered his troops dispatched to the western capital for autumn frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianqi had surrendered Huai West only a few months before when an edict ordered his troops sent west for autumn frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 仙奇遣都知兵馬使蘇浦悉將淮西精兵五千人以行。

translations.literal: Xianqi sent Chief Military Commissioner Su Pu to lead all five thousand elite Huai West troops on the march.
translations.idiomatic: Xianqi sent Chief Military Commissioner Su Pu to lead all five thousand elite Huai West troops on the march.

sentences.zh: 會仙奇為吳少誠所殺，少誠密遣人召門槍兵馬使吳法超等使引兵歸。

translations.literal: Just then Xianqi was killed by Wu Shaocheng; Shaocheng secretly sent men to summon Gate-Spear military commissioner Wu Fachao and others to lead the troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Xianqi was killed by Wu Shaocheng. Shaocheng secretly sent men to summon Gate-Spear military commissioner Wu Fachao and others to lead the troops back.

sentences.zh: 浦不之知。

translations.literal: Pu knew nothing of this.
translations.idiomatic: Pu knew nothing of this.

sentences.zh: 法超等引步騎四千自鄜州叛歸，渾瑊使其將白娑勒追之，反為所敗。

translations.literal: Fachao and others led four thousand infantry and cavalry in mutiny from Bin Prefecture back home; Hun Jian sent his general Bai Suole to pursue them but was instead defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Fachao and others led four thousand infantry and cavalry in mutiny from Bin Prefecture homeward. Hun Jian sent his general Bai Suole to pursue them but was defeated instead.

sentences.zh: 丙午，上急遣中使敕陝虢觀察使李泌發兵防遏，勿令濟河。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the emperor urgently dispatched an imperial messenger ordering Shan-Guo Observation Commissioner Li Bi to mobilize troops to block them and not allow them to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the emperor urgently sent an imperial messenger ordering Shan-Guo Observation Commissioner Li Bi to mobilize troops to block them and not let them cross the river.

sentences.zh: 泌遣押牙唐英岸將兵趣靈寶，淮西兵已陳於河南矣。

translations.literal: Bi sent his yamen officer Tang Ying'an with troops toward Lingbao—the Huai West army was already drawn up south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Bi sent his yamen officer Tang Ying'an with troops toward Lingbao. The Huai West army was already drawn up south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 泌乃命靈寶給其食，淮西兵亦不敢剽掠。

translations.literal: Bi then ordered Lingbao to supply them with food, and the Huai West troops did not dare to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Bi then ordered Lingbao to supply them with food, and the Huai West troops did not dare to plunder.

sentences.zh: 明日，宿陝西七里。

translations.literal: The next day they encamped seven li west of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they encamped seven li west of Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 泌不給其食，遣將將選士四百人分為二隊，伏於太原倉之隘道，令之曰：「賊十隊過，東伏則大呼擊之，西伏亦大呼應之，勿遮道，勿留行，常讓以半道，隨而擊之。」

translations.literal: Bi did not supply them with food. He sent a general to lead four hundred picked men in two teams to lie in ambush in the narrow pass at Taiyuan Granary, instructing them: "When ten enemy columns have passed, the eastern ambush is to shout and strike; the western ambush is also to shout in response. Do not block the road; do not hold up their march. Always yield half the road, then strike as you follow."
translations.idiomatic: Bi did not supply them with food. He sent a general to lead four hundred picked men in two teams to lie in ambush in the narrow pass at Taiyuan Granary, instructing them, "When ten enemy columns have passed, the eastern ambush is to shout and strike; the western ambush is also to shout in response. Do not block the road. Do not hold up their march. Always yield half the road, then strike as you follow."

sentences.zh: 又遣虞侯集近村少年各持弓、刀、瓦石躡賊後，聞呼亦應而追之。

translations.literal: He also sent runners to gather youths from nearby villages, each armed with bow, knife, and stones, to trail behind the enemy; when they heard the shouts they too responded and pursued.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent runners to gather youths from nearby villages, each armed with bow, knife, and stones, to trail behind the enemy. When they heard the shouts, they too responded and pursued.

sentences.zh: 又遣唐英岸將千五百人夜出南門，陳於澗北。

translations.literal: He also sent Tang Ying'an with fifteen hundred men out the south gate at night to draw up north of the stream.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Tang Ying'an with fifteen hundred men out the south gate at night to draw up north of the stream.

sentences.zh: 明日四鼓，淮西兵起行入隘，兩伏發。

translations.literal: At the fourth watch the next day, the Huai West troops set out and entered the pass; both ambushes sprang.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth watch the next day, the Huai West troops set out and entered the pass. Both ambushes sprang.

sentences.zh: 賊眾驚亂，且戰且走，死者四之一。

translations.literal: The enemy force panicked and scattered, fighting as they fled; one in four died.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy force panicked and scattered, fighting as they fled. One in four was killed.

sentences.zh: 進遇唐英岸，邀而擊之，賊眾大敗，擒其騾軍兵馬使張崇獻。

translations.literal: Advancing, they met Tang Ying'an, who intercepted and struck them; the enemy force was routed, and their Mule Army military commissioner Zhang Chongxian was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing, they met Tang Ying'an, who intercepted and struck them. The enemy force was routed, and their Mule Army military commissioner Zhang Chongxian was captured.

sentences.zh: 泌以賊必分兵自山路南遁，又遣都將燕子楚將兵四百自炭竇谷趣長水。

translations.literal: Bi judged that the enemy would surely split forces and flee south by mountain paths; he also sent Chief Commander Yan Zichu with four hundred men through Tandou Valley toward Changshui.
translations.idiomatic: Bi judged that the enemy would surely split forces and flee south by mountain paths. He also sent Chief Commander Yan Zichu with four hundred men through Tandou Valley toward Changshui.

sentences.zh: 賊二日不食，屢戰皆敗，英岸追至永寧東，賊皆潰入山谷。

translations.literal: The enemy had gone two days without food, lost battle after battle; Ying'an pursued them to east of Yongning, and the enemy all fled in rout into the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had gone two days without food and lost battle after battle. Ying'an pursued them to east of Yongning, and the enemy all fled in rout into the valleys.

sentences.zh: 吳法超果帥其眾太半趣長水，燕子楚擊之，斬法超，殺其士卒三分之二。

translations.literal: Wu Fachao indeed led the greater part of his force toward Changshui; Yan Zichu struck them, beheaded Fachao, and killed two-thirds of his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fachao indeed led the greater part of his force toward Changshui. Yan Zichu struck them, beheaded Fachao, and killed two-thirds of his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 上以陝兵少，發神策軍步騎五千往助泌，至赤水，聞賊已破而還。

translations.literal: Because Shan troops were few, the emperor dispatched five thousand Shence Army infantry and cavalry to assist Bi; they reached Chishui, heard the enemy was already broken, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shan troops were few, the emperor dispatched five thousand Shence Army infantry and cavalry to assist Bi. They reached Chishui, heard the enemy was already broken, and returned.

sentences.zh: 上命劉玄佐乘驛歸汴，以詔書緣道誘之，得百三十餘人，至汴州，盡殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Liu Xuanzuo to ride post-horses back to Bian and, with edicts posted along the route, lure them in; he got more than one hundred thirty men and, upon reaching Bian Prefecture, had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Liu Xuanzuo to ride post-horses back to Bian and, with edicts posted along the route, lure them in. He got more than one hundred thirty men and, upon reaching Bian Prefecture, had them all killed.

sentences.zh: 其潰兵在道，復為村民所殺，得至蔡者，才四十七人。

translations.literal: The scattered troops still on the road were again killed by villagers; only forty-seven reached Cai.
translations.idiomatic: The scattered troops still on the road were again killed by villagers. Only forty-seven reached Cai.

sentences.zh: 吳少誠以其少，悉斬之以聞。

translations.literal: Wu Shaocheng, finding them too few, had them all beheaded and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaocheng, finding them too few, had them all beheaded and reported it.

sentences.zh: 且遣使以幣謝李泌，為其破叛卒也。

translations.literal: He also sent an envoy with gifts to thank Li Bi for breaking the mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent an envoy with gifts to thank Li Bi for breaking the mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 泌執張崇獻等六十餘人送京師，詔悉腰斬於鄜州軍門，以令防秋之眾。

translations.literal: Bi detained Zhang Chongxian and more than sixty others and sent them to the capital; an edict ordered them all beheaded at the waist at the army gate in Bin Prefecture, as a warning to the autumn-defense troops.
translations.idiomatic: Bi detained Zhang Chongxian and more than sixty others and sent them to the capital. An edict ordered them all beheaded at the waist at the army gate in Bin Prefecture, as a warning to the autumn-defense troops.

sentences.zh: 初，雲南王閤羅鳳陷巂州，獲西瀘令鄭回。

translations.literal: Earlier, the King of Yunnan, Piluoge, took Xi Prefecture and captured Xilu Prefect Zheng Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Piluoge, king of Yunnan, took Xi Prefecture and captured Xilu Prefect Zheng Hui.

sentences.zh: 回，相州人，通經術，閤羅鳳愛重之。

translations.literal: Hui was a man of Xiang Prefecture, versed in the classics; Piluoge cherished and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was from Xiang Prefecture and versed in the classics. Piluoge cherished and honored him.

sentences.zh: 其子鳳迦異及孫異牟尋、曾孫尋夢湊皆師事之，每授學，回得撻之。

translations.literal: His son Fengjiayi and grandson Yimouxun, and great-grandson Xunmengcou, all studied under him as disciples; whenever he taught, Hui was allowed to beat them.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fengjiayi, grandson Yimouxun, and great-grandson Xunmengcou all studied under him as disciples. Whenever he taught, Hui was allowed to beat them.

sentences.zh: 及異牟尋為王，以回為清平官。

translations.literal: When Yimouxun became king, he made Hui a Qingping official.
translations.idiomatic: When Yimouxun became king, he made Hui a Qingping official.

sentences.zh: 清平官者，蠻相也，凡有六人，而國事專決於回。

translations.literal: Qingping officials were barbarian chancellors—there were six in all—and state affairs were decided exclusively by Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Qingping officials were barbarian chancellors. There were six in all, and state affairs were decided exclusively by Hui.

sentences.zh: 五人者事回甚卑謹，有過，則回撻之。

translations.literal: The five others served Hui with great humility and care; if they erred, Hui beat them.
translations.idiomatic: The five others served Hui with great humility and care. If they erred, Hui beat them.

sentences.zh: 雲南有眾數十萬，吐蕃每入寇，常以雲南為前鋒，賦斂重數，又奪其險要立城堡，歲徵兵助防，雲南苦之。

translations.literal: Yunnan had a population of several hundred thousand; whenever the Tibetans raided, they always used Yunnan as vanguard, levied heavy taxes repeatedly, seized strategic points to build fortresses, and conscripted troops each year to help defend—Yunnan suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan had a population of several hundred thousand. Whenever the Tibetans raided, they always used Yunnan as vanguard, levied heavy taxes repeatedly, seized strategic points to build fortresses, and conscripted troops each year to help defend. Yunnan suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 回因說異牟尋復自歸於唐，曰：「中國尚禮義，有惠澤，無賦役。」

translations.literal: Hui therefore urged Yimouxun to return to allegiance to Tang, saying: "China honors ritual and righteousness, bestows gracious benefits, and imposes no levies or corvée."
translations.idiomatic: Hui therefore urged Yimouxun to return to allegiance to Tang, saying, "China honors ritual and righteousness, bestows gracious benefits, and imposes no levies or corvée."

sentences.zh: 異牟尋以為然，而無路自致，凡十餘年。

translations.literal: Yimouxun thought this correct, but had no way to reach Tang on his own—for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun thought this correct, but had no way to reach Tang on his own. This went on for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 及西川節度使韋皋至鎮，招撫境上群蠻，異牟尋潛遣人因諸蠻求內附。

translations.literal: When Xichuan Jiedushi Wei Gao arrived at his post, he recruited and pacified the barbarian tribes on the border; Yimouxun secretly sent men through the various tribes to seek submission.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Gao, military governor of Xichuan, arrived at his post, he recruited and pacified the barbarian tribes on the border. Yimouxun secretly sent men through the various tribes to seek submission.

sentences.zh: 皋奏：「今吐蕃棄好，暴亂鹽、夏，宜因雲南及八國生羌有歸化之心招納之，以離吐蕃之黨，分其勢。」

translations.literal: Gao memorialized: "Now the Tibetans have cast aside friendship and violently ravaged Yan and Xia. We should take advantage of Yunnan and the eight tribes of raw Qiang who wish to submit, recruit them, split the Tibetan faction, and divide their strength."
translations.idiomatic: Gao memorialized, "Now the Tibetans have cast aside friendship and violently ravaged Yan and Xia. We should take advantage of Yunnan and the eight tribes of raw Qiang who wish to submit, recruit them, split the Tibetan faction, and divide their strength."

sentences.zh: 上命皋先作邊將書以諭之，微觀其趣。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Gao first to write a frontier general's letter to instruct them and subtly observe their inclinations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Gao first to write a frontier general's letter to instruct them and subtly observe their inclinations.

sentences.zh: 張延賞與齊映有隙，映在諸相中頗稱敢言，上浸不悅。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanshang and Qi Ying were at odds; among the chief ministers Ying was known for speaking boldly, and the emperor gradually grew displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanshang and Qi Ying were at odds. Among the chief ministers, Ying was known for speaking boldly, and the emperor gradually grew displeased.

sentences.zh: 延賞言映非宰相器。

translations.literal: Yanshang said Ying was not material for a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang said Ying was not fit to be chief minister.

sentences.zh: 壬子，映貶夔州刺史。

translations.literal: On renzi, Ying was demoted to Prefect of Kui.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Ying was demoted to prefect of Kui.

sentences.zh: 劉滋羅為左散騎常侍，以兵部侍郎柳渾同平章事。

translations.literal: Liu Zi was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; Vice Minister of War Liu Hun was made co-chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zi was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, and Liu Hun, vice minister of war, was made co-chief minister.

sentences.zh: 韓滉性苛暴，方為上所任，言無不從，他相充位而已，百官群吏救過不贍。

translations.literal: Han Huang was by nature harsh and violent; just then he was trusted by the emperor and his every word was obeyed. The other chief ministers were mere placeholders, and officials and clerks at every level barely had time to remedy their faults.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang was by nature harsh and violent. Just then he was trusted by the emperor and his every word was obeyed. The other chief ministers were mere placeholders, and officials and clerks at every level barely had time to remedy their faults.

sentences.zh: 渾另為滉所引薦，正色讓之曰：「先相公以褊察為相，不滿歲而罷，今公又甚焉。

translations.literal: Liu Hun had been recommended by Huang. With stern countenance he reproached him, saying: "The former chief minister served as chancellor through petty suspicion and scrutiny; within less than a year he was dismissed. Now you have gone even further.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hun had been recommended by Huang. With stern countenance he reproached him, saying, "The former chief minister served as chancellor through petty suspicion and scrutiny. Within less than a year he was dismissed. Now you have gone even further.

sentences.zh: 奈何榜吏於省中，至有死者！

translations.literal: How can you flog clerks in the ministry until some have died!
translations.idiomatic: How can you flog clerks in the ministry until some have died!

sentences.zh: 且作福作威，豈人臣所宜！」

translations.literal: And to grant favors and wield power—how is that fitting for a subject minister!"
translations.idiomatic: And to grant favors and wield power—how is that fitting for a subject minister!"

sentences.zh: 滉愧，為之少霽威嚴。

translations.literal: Huang was ashamed and somewhat relaxed his severity on their account.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was ashamed and somewhat relaxed his severity on their account.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬戌，以檢校左庶子崔浣充入吐蕃使。

translations.literal: In the second month, on renxu, Cui Wan, acting Left Household Companion, was appointed envoy to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renxu, Cui Wan, acting Left Household Companion, was appointed envoy to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，鎮海節度使、同平章事、充江、淮轉運使韓滉薨。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Han Huang, military governor of Zhenhai, co-chief minister, and commissioner for Jiang-Huai transport, died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Han Huang, military governor of Zhenhai, co-chief minister, and commissioner for Jiang-Huai transport, died.

sentences.zh: 滉久在二浙，所辟僚佐，各隨其長，無不得人。

translations.literal: Huang had long served in the two Zhe regions. Among the staff he recruited, each was assigned according to his strengths, and none failed to find his proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Huang had long served in the two Zhe regions. Among the staff he recruited, each was assigned according to his strengths, and none failed to find his proper place.

sentences.zh: 嘗有故人子謁之，考其能，一無所長，滉與之宴，竟席，未嘗左右視及與並坐交言。

translations.literal: Once a friend's son came to see him. After testing his abilities, he found the man had no particular talent. Huang feasted with him; through the entire banquet he never once glanced to either side or spoke with him as an equal at the same seat.
translations.idiomatic: Once a friend's son came to see him. After testing his abilities, he found the man had no particular talent. Huang feasted with him. Through the entire banquet he never once glanced to either side or spoke with him as an equal at the same seat.

sentences.zh: 後數日，署為隨軍，使監庫門。

translations.literal: A few days later he appointed him as camp follower and had him oversee the storehouse gate.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he appointed him as camp follower and had him oversee the storehouse gate.

sentences.zh: 其人終日危坐，吏卒無敢妄出入者。

translations.literal: The man sat upright in formal posture all day long, and clerks and soldiers did not dare enter or leave without cause.
translations.idiomatic: The man sat upright in formal posture all day long, and clerks and soldiers did not dare enter or leave without cause.

sentences.zh: 分浙江東、西道為三：浙西，治潤州；

translations.literal: The Jiangsu-Zhejiang Eastern and Western circuits were divided into three: Western Zhe, administered from Run Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangsu-Zhejiang Eastern and Western circuits were divided into three: Western Zhe, administered from Run Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 浙東，治越州；

translations.literal: Eastern Zhe, administered from Yue Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Zhe, administered from Yue Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 宣、歙、池，治宣州；

translations.literal: Xuan, She, and Chi, administered from Xuan Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, She, and Chi, administered from Xuan Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 各置觀察使以領之。

translations.literal: each was given an observation commissioner to govern it.
translations.idiomatic: each was given an observation commissioner to govern it.

sentences.zh: 上以果州刺史白志貞為浙西觀察使，柳渾曰：「志貞，憸人，不可復用。」

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Bai Zhizhen, prefect of Guo, as observation commissioner of Western Zhe. Liu Hun said, "Zhizhen is a crafty man and must not be employed again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Bai Zhizhen, prefect of Guo, as observation commissioner of Western Zhe. Liu Hun said, "Zhizhen is a crafty man and must not be employed again."

sentences.zh: 會渾疾，不視事，辛巳，詔下，用之。

translations.literal: Just then Hun fell ill and ceased attending to affairs. On xinsi the edict was issued and Zhizhen was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Hun fell ill and ceased attending to affairs. On xinsi the edict was issued and Zhizhen was appointed.

sentences.zh: 渾疾間，遂乞骸骨，不許。

translations.literal: While Hun was ill he asked to retire on account of age, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: While Hun was ill he asked to retire on account of age, but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 甲申，葬昭德皇后於靖陵。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Empress Zhaode was buried at Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Empress Zhaode was buried at Jing Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁酉，以左庶子李銛充入吐蕃使。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingyou, Li Xian, Left Household Companion, was appointed envoy to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingyou, Li Xian, Left Household Companion, was appointed envoy to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 初，吐蕃尚結讚得鹽、夏州，各留千餘人戍之，退屯鳴沙。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Tibetan Shang Jiezan had taken Yan and Xia prefectures, leaving more than a thousand men to garrison each, then withdrew and encamped at Mingsha.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Tibetan Shang Jiezan had taken Yan and Xia prefectures, leaving more than a thousand men to garrison each, then withdrew and encamped at Mingsha.

sentences.zh: 自冬入春，羊馬多死。

translations.literal: From winter into spring, many sheep and horses died.
translations.idiomatic: From winter into spring, many sheep and horses died.

sentences.zh: 糧運不繼，又聞李晟克摧沙，馬燧、渾瑊等各舉兵臨之，大懼，屢遣使求和，上未之許。

translations.literal: Grain transport could not keep up. They also heard that Li Sheng had taken Cuisha, and Ma Sui, Hun Jian, and others each mobilized troops and pressed upon them. Greatly alarmed, they repeatedly sent envoys seeking peace, but the emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Grain transport could not keep up. They also heard that Li Sheng had taken Cuisha, and Ma Sui, Hun Jian, and others each mobilized troops and pressed upon them. Greatly alarmed, they repeatedly sent envoys seeking peace, but the emperor did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使卑辭厚禮求和於馬燧，且請修清水之盟而歸侵地，使者相繼於路。

translations.literal: They then sent envoys with humble words and lavish gifts to seek peace from Ma Sui, also requesting restoration of the Qingshui covenant and return of the seized territory. Envoys followed one another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: They then sent envoys with humble words and lavish gifts to seek peace from Ma Sui, also requesting restoration of the Qingshui covenant and return of the seized territory. Envoys followed one another on the road.

sentences.zh: 燧信其言，留屯石州，不復濟河，為之請於朝。

translations.literal: Sui believed their words. He remained encamped at Shi Prefecture and no longer crossed the river, requesting this on their behalf at court.
translations.idiomatic: Sui believed their words. He remained encamped at Shi Prefecture and no longer crossed the river, requesting this on their behalf at court.

sentences.zh: 李晟曰：「戎狄無信，不如擊之。」

translations.literal: Li Sheng said, "The barbarians are faithless; it is better to strike them."
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng said, "The barbarians are faithless; it is better to strike them."

sentences.zh: 韓游瑰曰：「吐蕃弱則求盟，強則入寇，今深入塞內而求盟，此必詐也！」

translations.literal: Han Yougui said, "When Tibet is weak it seeks alliance; when strong it raids. Now, having penetrated deep inside the frontier yet seeking alliance—this must be deception!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui said, "When Tibet is weak it seeks alliance; when strong it raids. Now, having penetrated deep inside the frontier yet seeking alliance—this must be deception!"

sentences.zh: 韓滉曰：「今兩河無虞，若城原、鄯、洮、渭四州，使李晟、劉玄佐之徒將十萬眾戍之，河、湟二十餘州可復也。

translations.literal: Han Huang said, "Now the two He regions are secure. If we fortify the four prefectures of Yuan, Shan, Tao, and Wei, and have Li Sheng, Liu Xuanzuo, and the like lead a hundred thousand men to garrison them, more than twenty prefectures of the He and Huang regions can be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang said, "Now the two He regions are secure. If we fortify the four prefectures of Yuan, Shan, Tao, and Wei, and have Li Sheng, Liu Xuanzuo, and the like lead a hundred thousand men to garrison them, more than twenty prefectures of the He and Huang regions can be recovered.

sentences.zh: 其資糧之費，臣請主辦。」

translations.literal: As for the cost of provisions, your subject requests to take charge of it."
translations.idiomatic: As for the cost of provisions, your subject requests to take charge of it."

sentences.zh: 上由是不聽燧計，趣使進兵。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore did not heed Sui's plan and urged him to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore did not heed Sui's plan and urged him to advance.

sentences.zh: 燧請與吐蕃使論頰熱俱入朝論之，會滉薨，燧、延賞皆與晟有隙，欲反其謀，爭言和親便。

translations.literal: Sui requested that the Tibetan envoy Lun Zanre accompany him to court to discuss the matter. Just then Huang died. Sui and Yanshang both bore grudges against Sheng and wished to overturn his plan; each argued that marriage alliance would be advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Sui requested that the Tibetan envoy Lun Zanre accompany him to court to discuss the matter. Just then Huang died. Sui and Yanshang both bore grudges against Sheng and wished to overturn his plan. Each argued that marriage alliance would be advantageous.

sentences.zh: 上亦恨回紇，欲與吐蕃和，共擊之，得二人言，正會己意，計遂定。

translations.literal: The emperor also resented the Uyghurs and wished to reconcile with Tibet to jointly attack them. Hearing the two men's words matched his own intent, the plan was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also resented the Uyghurs and wished to reconcile with Tibet to jointly attack them. Hearing the two men's words matched his own intent, the plan was settled.

sentences.zh: 延賞數言「晟不宜久典兵，請以鄭雲逵代之。」

translations.literal: Yanshang repeatedly said, "Sheng should not hold military command for long. I request that Zheng Yunkui replace him."
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang repeatedly said, "Sheng should not hold military command for long. I request that Zheng Yunkui replace him."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「當令自擇代者。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "He should choose his own replacement."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He should choose his own replacement."

sentences.zh: 乃謂晟曰：「朕以百姓之故，與吐蕃和親決矣。

translations.literal: He then said to Sheng, "For the sake of the people, I have decided on marriage alliance with Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Sheng, "For the sake of the people, I have decided on marriage alliance with Tibet.

sentences.zh: 大臣既與吐蕃有怨，不可復之鳳翔，宜留朝廷，朝夕輔朕，自擇一人可代鳳翔者。

translations.literal: Since you, a chief minister, bear grudges against Tibet, you cannot return to Fengxiang. You should remain at court, assisting me morning and evening. Choose for yourself someone who can replace you at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Since you, a chief minister, bear grudges against Tibet, you cannot return to Fengxiang. You should remain at court, assisting me morning and evening. Choose for yourself someone who can replace you at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 晟薦都虞候邢君牙。

translations.literal: Sheng recommended Chief Adjutant Xing Junya.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng recommended Chief Adjutant Xing Junya.

sentences.zh: 君牙，樂壽人也。

translations.literal: Junya was a man of Leshou.
translations.idiomatic: Junya was a man of Leshou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以君牙為鳳翔尹團練使。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Junya was made prefect and regimentation commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Junya was made prefect and regimentation commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 丁未，加晟太尉、中書令，勳、封如故；

translations.literal: On dingwei, Sheng was promoted to Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat; his honors and fief remained unchanged;
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Sheng was promoted to Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat; his honors and fief remained unchanged;

sentences.zh: 餘悉罷之。

translations.literal: all other posts were removed.
translations.idiomatic: all other posts were removed.

sentences.zh: 晟在鳳翔，嘗謂僚佐曰：「魏徵好直諫，余竊慕之。」

translations.literal: While Sheng was at Fengxiang, he once said to his staff, "Wei Zheng loved to speak blunt remonstrance; I have privately admired that."
translations.idiomatic: While Sheng was at Fengxiang, he once said to his staff, "Wei Zheng loved to speak blunt remonstrance; I have privately admired that."

sentences.zh: 行軍司馬李叔度曰：「此乃儒者所為，非勳德所宜。」

translations.literal: Military Affairs Secretary Li Shudu said, "That is what scholars do—it is not fitting for a man of merit and virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Military Affairs Secretary Li Shudu said, "That is what scholars do—it is not fitting for a man of merit and virtue."

sentences.zh: 晟斂容曰：「司馬失言。

translations.literal: Sheng composed his expression and said, "The Secretary spoke amiss.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng composed his expression and said, "The Secretary spoke amiss.

sentences.zh: 晟任兼將相，知朝廷得失不言，何以為臣！」

translations.literal: Sheng holds both generalship and chancellorship. If knowing the court's gains and losses I do not speak, how can I be a minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng holds both generalship and chancellorship. If knowing the court's gains and losses I do not speak, how can I be a minister!"

sentences.zh: 叔度慚而退。

translations.literal: Shudu withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Shudu withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 及在朝廷，上有所顧問，極言無隱。

translations.literal: When later at court, whenever the emperor consulted him, he spoke with utmost candor and held nothing back.
translations.idiomatic: When later at court, whenever the emperor consulted him, he spoke with utmost candor and held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 性沉密，未嘗洩於人。

translations.literal: By nature he was deep and reserved; he never leaked matters to others.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was deep and reserved; he never leaked matters to others.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，馬燧入朝。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Ma Sui entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Ma Sui entered court.

sentences.zh: 燧既來，諸軍皆閉壁不戰，尚結贊遽自鳴沙引歸，其眾乏馬，多徒行者。

translations.literal: Once Sui had come, all armies closed their walls and did not fight. Shang Jiezan hastily led his forces back from Mingsha. His troops lacked horses, and many went on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sui had come, all armies closed their walls and did not fight. Shang Jiezan hastily led his forces back from Mingsha. His troops lacked horses, and many went on foot.

sentences.zh: 崔浣見尚結贊，責以負約。

translations.literal: Cui Wan met Shang Jiezan and reproached him for breaking his pledge.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wan met Shang Jiezan and reproached him for breaking his pledge.

sentences.zh: 尚結贊曰：「吐蕃破朱泚，未獲賞，是以來，而諸州各城守，無由自達。

translations.literal: Shang Jiezan said, "Tibet helped defeat Zhu Ci yet received no reward. That is why we came. But each prefecture held its walls, and we had no way to reach you on our own.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Jiezan said, "Tibet helped defeat Zhu Ci yet received no reward. That is why we came. But each prefecture held its walls, and we had no way to reach you on our own.

sentences.zh: 鹽、夏守者以城授我而遁，非我取之也。

translations.literal: The garrisons of Yan and Xia surrendered their cities to us and fled—they were not taken by force.
translations.idiomatic: The garrisons of Yan and Xia surrendered their cities to us and fled—they were not taken by force.

sentences.zh: 今明公來，欲踐修舊好，固吐蕃之願也。

translations.literal: Now that you have come, seeking to restore the old friendship is indeed Tibet's wish.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have come, seeking to restore the old friendship is indeed Tibet's wish.

sentences.zh: 今吐蕃將相以下來者二十一人，渾侍中嘗與之共事，知其忠信。

translations.literal: Now twenty-one Tibetan generals and ministers have come down. Vice Minister Hun once worked with them and knows them to be loyal and trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Now twenty-one Tibetan generals and ministers have come down. Vice Minister Hun once worked with them and knows them to be loyal and trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 靈州節度使杜希全、涇原節度使李觀皆信厚聞於異域，請使之主盟。」

translations.literal: Military governor of Ling Prefecture Du Xiquan and military governor of Jingyuan Li Guan are both known in distant lands for faith and kindness. We ask that they preside over the covenant."
translations.idiomatic: Military governor of Ling Prefecture Du Xiquan and military governor of Jingyuan Li Guan are both known in distant lands for faith and kindness. We ask that they preside over the covenant."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙寅，浣至長安。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingyin, Wan reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on bingyin, Wan reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以浣為鴻臚卿，復使入吐蕃語尚結贊曰：「希全守靈，不可出境，李觀已改官，今遣渾瑊盟於清水。」

translations.literal: On xinwei, Wan was made Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and again sent into Tibet to tell Shang Jiezan, "Xiquan holds Ling and cannot leave the frontier. Li Guan has changed posts. Now Hun Jian is being sent to covenant at Qingshui."
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Wan was made Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and again sent into Tibet to tell Shang Jiezan, "Xiquan holds Ling and cannot leave the frontier. Li Guan has changed posts. Now Hun Jian is being sent to covenant at Qingshui."

sentences.zh: 且令先歸鹽、夏二州。

translations.literal: He was also ordered first to return the two prefectures of Yan and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered first to return the two prefectures of Yan and Xia.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲申，渾自咸陽入朝，以為清水會盟使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiashen, Hun returned to court from Xianyang and was appointed covenant envoy at Qingshui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiashen, Hun returned to court from Xianyang and was appointed covenant envoy at Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以兵部尚書崔漢衡為副使，司封員外郎鄭叔矩為判官，特進宋奉朝為都監。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Vice Minister of War Cui Hanheng was made deputy envoy, Ministry of Rites outer-section clerk Zheng Shuju was made judge, and Special Advanced Song Fengchao was made chief supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Vice Minister of War Cui Hanheng was made deputy envoy, Ministry of Rites outer-section clerk Zheng Shuju was made judge, and Special Advanced Song Fengchao was made chief supervisor.

sentences.zh: 己丑，瑊將二萬餘人赴盟所。

translations.literal: On jichou, Jian led more than twenty thousand men to the covenant site.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Jian led more than twenty thousand men to the covenant site.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，尚結贊遣其屬論泣贊來言：「清水非吉地，請盟於原州之土梨樹，既盟而歸鹽、夏二州。」

translations.literal: On yisi, Shang Jiezan sent his subordinate Lun Qizan to say, "Qingshui is not an auspicious place. We ask to covenant at Tuli Tree in Yuan Prefecture. Once the covenant is made, we will return the two prefectures of Yan and Xia."
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Shang Jiezan sent his subordinate Lun Qizan to say, "Qingshui is not an auspicious place. We ask to covenant at Tuli Tree in Yuan Prefecture. Once the covenant is made, we will return the two prefectures of Yan and Xia."

sentences.zh: 上皆許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted all of this.

sentences.zh: 神策將馬有麟奏：「土梨樹多阻險，恐吐蕃設伏兵，不如平涼川坦夷。」

translations.literal: Shence general Ma Youlin memorialized, "Tuli Tree is full of rugged defiles. I fear Tibet may set an ambush. It would be better at the open ground of Pingliang Stream."
translations.idiomatic: Shence general Ma Youlin memorialized, "Tuli Tree is full of rugged defiles. I fear Tibet may set an ambush. It would be better at the open ground of Pingliang Stream."

sentences.zh: 時論泣贊已還，丁未，遣使追告之。

translations.literal: By then Lun Qizan had already returned. On dingwei a messenger was sent to catch up and inform him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Lun Qizan had already returned. On dingwei a messenger was sent to catch up and inform him.

sentences.zh: 申蔡留後吳少誠，繕兵完城，欲拒朝命，判官鄭常、大將楊冀謀逐之，詐為手詔賜諸將申州刺史張伯元等。

translations.literal: Wu Shaocheng, acting commissioner of Shen-Cai, repaired arms and completed fortifications, intending to resist the court's orders. Judge Zheng Chang and general Yang Ji plotted to drive him out. They forged an imperial handwritten edict to bestow on generals including Shen Prefecture prefect Zhang Boyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaocheng, acting commissioner of Shen-Cai, repaired arms and completed fortifications, intending to resist the court's orders. Judge Zheng Chang and general Yang Ji plotted to drive him out. They forged an imperial handwritten edict to bestow on generals including Shen Prefecture prefect Zhang Boyuan.

sentences.zh: 事洩，少誠殺常、冀、伯元。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, Shaocheng killed Chang, Ji, and Boyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was exposed, Shaocheng killed Chang, Ji, and Boyuan.

sentences.zh: 大將宋旻、曹濟奔長安。

translations.literal: Generals Song Min and Cao Ji fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Song Min and Cao Ji fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 閏月，己未，韋皋復與東蠻和義王苴那時書，使詗伺導達雲南。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on jiwei, Wei Gao again wrote to Junaishi, king of the Eastern Man and Prince of Heyi, having scouts guide the message through to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on jiwei, Wei Gao again wrote to Junaishi, king of the Eastern Man and Prince of Heyi, having scouts guide the message through to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 庚申，大省州、縣官員，收其祿以給戰士，張延賞之謀也。

translations.literal: On gengshen there was a great reduction of prefecture and county officials; their salaries were taken to supply the soldiers—this was Zhang Yanshang's plan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen there was a great reduction of prefecture and county officials; their salaries were taken to supply the soldiers. This was Zhang Yanshang's plan.

sentences.zh: 時新除官千五百人，而當減者千餘人，怨嗟盈路。

translations.literal: At the time fifteen hundred men had just been newly appointed, while more than a thousand were to be reduced. Resentful complaints filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: At the time fifteen hundred men had just been newly appointed, while more than a thousand were to be reduced. Resentful complaints filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 初，韓滉薦劉玄佐可使將兵復河、湟，上以問玄佐，玄佐亦贊成之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han Huang had recommended Liu Xuanzuo as capable of leading troops to recover the He and Huang regions. The emperor asked Xuanzuo, and Xuanzuo also endorsed the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han Huang had recommended Liu Xuanzuo as capable of leading troops to recover the He and Huang regions. The emperor asked Xuanzuo, and Xuanzuo also endorsed the plan.

sentences.zh: 滉薨，玄佐奏言：「吐蕃方強，未可與爭。」

translations.literal: When Huang died, Xuanzuo memorialized, "Tibet is presently strong; we cannot contend with it."
translations.idiomatic: When Huang died, Xuanzuo memorialized, "Tibet is presently strong; we cannot contend with it."

sentences.zh: 上遣中使勞問玄佐，玄佐臥而受命。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an imperial messenger to express sympathy and inquire of Xuanzuo. Xuanzuo received the command while lying in bed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an imperial messenger to express sympathy and inquire of Xuanzuo. Xuanzuo received the command while lying in bed.

sentences.zh: 張延賞知玄佐不可用，奏以河、湟事委李抱真，抱真亦固辭。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanshang knew Xuanzuo could not be used and memorialized to entrust the He and Huang affair to Li Baozhen. Baozhen also firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanshang knew Xuanzuo could not be used and memorialized to entrust the He and Huang affair to Li Baozhen. Baozhen also firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 皆由延賞罷李晟兵柄，故武臣皆憤怒解體，不肯為用故也。

translations.literal: This was all because Yanshang had stripped Li Sheng of military authority, so military men were furious and demoralized and refused to be employed.
translations.idiomatic: This was all because Yanshang had stripped Li Sheng of military authority, so military men were furious and demoralized and refused to be employed.

sentences.zh: 上以襄、鄧扼淮西衝要，癸亥，以荊南節度使曹王皋為山南東道節度使，以襄、鄧、復、郢、安、隨、唐七州隸之。

translations.literal: Because Xiang and Deng guarded the strategic point against Huai West, on guihai Cao Wang Gao, military governor of Jingnan, was made military governor of Shannan East Circuit, and the seven prefectures of Xiang, Deng, Fu, Ying, An, Sui, and Tang were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiang and Deng guarded the strategic point against Huai West, on guihai Cao Wang Gao, military governor of Jingnan, was made military governor of Shannan East Circuit, and the seven prefectures of Xiang, Deng, Fu, Ying, An, Sui, and Tang were placed under him.

sentences.zh: 渾瑊之發長安也，李晟深戒之，以盟所為備不可不嚴。

translations.literal: When Hun Jian was setting out from Chang'an, Li Sheng earnestly warned him that preparations at the covenant site could not be lax.
translations.idiomatic: When Hun Jian was setting out from Chang'an, Li Sheng earnestly warned him that preparations at the covenant site could not be lax.

sentences.zh: 張延賞言於上曰：「晟不欲盟好之成，故戒瑊以嚴備。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanshang said to the emperor, "Sheng does not want the alliance to succeed, therefore he warned Jian to take strict precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanshang said to the emperor, "Sheng does not want the alliance to succeed, therefore he warned Jian to take strict precautions.

sentences.zh: 我有疑彼之形，則彼亦疑我矣，盟何由成！」

translations.literal: If we show suspicion of them, they will also suspect us—how can a covenant be concluded!"
translations.idiomatic: If we show suspicion of them, they will also suspect us—how can a covenant be concluded!"

sentences.zh: 上乃召瑊，切戒以推誠待虜，勿自為猜貳以阻虜情。

translations.literal: The emperor then summoned Jian and sternly admonished him to treat the barbarians with sincerity and not arouse mutual suspicion that would obstruct the barbarians' goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then summoned Jian and sternly admonished him to treat the barbarians with sincerity and not arouse mutual suspicion that would obstruct the barbarians' goodwill.

sentences.zh: 瑊奏吐蕃決以辛未盟，延賞集百官，以瑊表稱詔示之曰：「李太尉謂吐蕃和好必不成，此渾侍中表也，盟日定矣。」

translations.literal: Jian reported that Tibet had settled on xinwei for the covenant. Yanshang assembled the hundred officials, displayed Jian's memorial styled as an imperial edict, and said, "Grand Marshal Li said a Tibetan reconciliation would certainly fail. This is Vice Minister Hun's memorial—the day of covenant is fixed."
translations.idiomatic: Jian reported that Tibet had settled on xinwei for the covenant. Yanshang assembled the hundred officials, displayed Jian's memorial styled as an imperial edict, and said, "Grand Marshal Li said a Tibetan reconciliation would certainly fail. This is Vice Minister Hun's memorial—the day of covenant is fixed."

sentences.zh: 晟聞之，泣謂所親曰：「吾生長西陲，備諳虜情，所以論奏，但恥朝廷為犬戎所侮耳！」

translations.literal: When Sheng heard of it, he wept and said to those close to him, "I grew up on the western frontier and am thoroughly familiar with barbarian dispositions. The reason I argued and memorialized was only that I was shamed to see the court humiliated by the Dog Barbarians!"
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng heard of it, he wept and said to those close to him, "I grew up on the western frontier and am thoroughly familiar with barbarian dispositions. The reason I argued and memorialized was only that I was shamed to see the court humiliated by the Dog Barbarians!"

sentences.zh: 上始命駱元光屯潘原，韓游瑰屯洛口，以為瑊援。

translations.literal: The emperor first ordered Luo Yuanguang to encamp at Panyuan and Han Yougui to encamp at Luokou, as reinforcement for Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first ordered Luo Yuanguang to encamp at Panyuan and Han Yougui to encamp at Luokou, as reinforcement for Jian.

sentences.zh: 元光謂瑊曰：「潘原距盟所且七十里，公有急，元光何從知之！

translations.literal: Yuanguang said to Jian, "Panyuan is nearly seventy li from the covenant site. If you are in distress, how is Yuanguang to know!
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguang said to Jian, "Panyuan is nearly seventy li from the covenant site. If you are in distress, how is Yuanguang to know!

sentences.zh: 請與公俱。」

translations.literal: I ask to accompany you."
translations.idiomatic: I ask to accompany you."

sentences.zh: 瑊以詔指固止之。

translations.literal: Jian firmly stopped him, citing the imperial instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Jian firmly stopped him, citing the imperial instructions.

sentences.zh: 元光不從，與瑊連營相次，距明所三十餘里。

translations.literal: Yuanguang would not obey. He and Jian encamped in succession, more than thirty li from the covenant site.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguang would not obey. He and Jian encamped in succession, more than thirty li from the covenant site.

sentences.zh: 元光壕柵深固，瑊壕柵皆可逾也。

translations.literal: Yuanguang's moats and palisades were deep and strong; Jian's could all be crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguang's moats and palisades were deep and strong; Jian's could all be crossed.

sentences.zh: 元光伏兵於營西，韓游瑰亦遣五百騎伏於其側，曰：「若有變，則汝曹西趣柏泉以分其勢。」

translations.literal: Yuanguang hid troops west of his camp. Han Yougui also sent five hundred cavalry to lie in ambush on the flank, saying, "If there is trouble, then you men ride west toward Baiquan to divide their force."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguang hid troops west of his camp. Han Yougui also sent five hundred cavalry to lie in ambush on the flank, saying, "If there is trouble, then you men ride west toward Baiquan to divide their force."

sentences.zh: 尚結贊與瑊約，各以甲士三千人列於壇之東西，常服者四百人從至壇下，辛未，將盟，尚結贊又請各遣游騎數十更相覘索，瑊皆許之。

translations.literal: Shang Jiezan and Jian agreed that each would array three thousand armored soldiers east and west of the altar; four hundred in ordinary dress would follow down to the altar. On xinwei, when they were about to covenant, Shang Jiezan again asked that each side send several dozen scouting horsemen to reconnoiter each other in turn. Jian permitted everything.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Jiezan and Jian agreed that each would array three thousand armored soldiers east and west of the altar; four hundred in ordinary dress would follow down to the altar. On xinwei, when they were about to covenant, Shang Jiezan again asked that each side send several dozen scouting horsemen to reconnoiter each other in turn. Jian permitted everything.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃伏精騎數萬於壇西，游騎貫穿唐軍，出入無禁。

translations.literal: Tibet hid tens of thousands of elite cavalry west of the altar. Scouting horsemen pierced through the Tang army and came and went without restriction.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet hid tens of thousands of elite cavalry west of the altar. Scouting horsemen pierced through the Tang army and came and went without restriction.

sentences.zh: 唐騎入虜軍，悉為所擒，瑊等皆不知，入幕，易禮服。

translations.literal: Tang horsemen who entered the barbarian army were all captured. Jian and the others knew nothing of it. They entered the pavilion and changed into ceremonial dress.
translations.idiomatic: Tang horsemen who entered the barbarian army were all captured. Jian and the others knew nothing of it. They entered the pavilion and changed into ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 虜伐鼓三聲，大噪而至，殺宋奉朝等於幕中。

translations.literal: The barbarians beat the drum three times, came with a great uproar, and killed Song Fengchao and others inside the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians beat the drum three times, came with a great uproar, and killed Song Fengchao and others inside the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 瑊自幕後出，偶得它馬乘之，伏鬣入其銜，馳十餘里，銜方及馬口，故矢過其背而不傷。

translations.literal: Jian emerged from behind the pavilion, by chance got another horse and mounted it. The mane lay flat against the bit in its mouth. He galloped more than ten li before the bit reached the horse's mouth. Therefore arrows passed over his back without wounding him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian emerged from behind the pavilion, by chance got another horse and mounted it. The mane lay flat against the bit in its mouth. He galloped more than ten li before the bit reached the horse's mouth. Therefore arrows passed over his back without wounding him.

sentences.zh: 唐將卒皆東走，虜縱兵追擊，或殺或擒之，死者數百人，擒者千餘人，崔漢衡為虜騎所擒。

translations.literal: Tang generals and soldiers all fled east. The barbarians loosed their troops in pursuit; some they killed, some they captured. Several hundred died; more than a thousand were captured. Cui Hanheng was seized by barbarian cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Tang generals and soldiers all fled east. The barbarians loosed their troops in pursuit; some they killed, some they captured. Several hundred died; more than a thousand were captured. Cui Hanheng was seized by barbarian cavalry.

sentences.zh: 渾瑊至其營，則將卒皆遁去，營空矣。

translations.literal: When Hun Jian reached his camp, the generals and soldiers had all fled. The camp was empty.
translations.idiomatic: When Hun Jian reached his camp, the generals and soldiers had all fled. The camp was empty.

sentences.zh: 駱元光發伏成陳以待之，虜追騎愕眙。

translations.literal: Luo Yuanguang deployed his ambush and formed battle lines to await them. The pursuing barbarian cavalry stared in astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yuanguang deployed his ambush and formed battle lines to await them. The pursuing barbarian cavalry stared in astonishment.

sentences.zh: 瑊入元光營，追騎顧見邠寧軍西馳，乃還。

translations.literal: Jian entered Yuanguang's camp. The pursuing horsemen, looking back, saw the Binning army galloping west and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Jian entered Yuanguang's camp. The pursuing horsemen, glancing back, saw the Binning army riding west and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 元光以輜重資瑊，與瑊收散卒，勒兵整陳而還。

translations.literal: Yuanguang supplied Jian with baggage train and stores. With Jian he gathered scattered soldiers, marshaled troops, set ranks in order, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguang shared supplies and baggage with Jian; together they rallied scattered troops, re-formed the army, and withdrew in good order.

sentences.zh: 是日上臨朝，謂諸相曰：「今日和戎息兵，社稷之福。」

translations.literal: That day the Emperor attended court and said to the chief ministers, "Today peace with the Rong and cessation of arms are a blessing for the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: That day the Emperor held court and told the chief ministers, "Today's peace with the barbarians and the laying down of arms are a blessing for the realm."

sentences.zh: 馬燧曰：「然。」

translations.literal: Ma Sui said, "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui said, "Indeed."

sentences.zh: 柳渾曰：「戎狄，豺狼也，非盟誓可結。

translations.literal: Liu Hun said, "The Rong and Di are wolves; they cannot be bound by oath and covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hun said, "The barbarians are wolves; no oath or covenant can bind them.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，臣竊憂之！」

translations.literal: Today's affair—your subject privately fears it!"
translations.idiomatic: As for what happened today, I am deeply worried!"

sentences.zh: 李晟曰：「誠如渾言。」

translations.literal: Li Sheng said, "It is truly as Hun says."
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng said, "Hun is right."

sentences.zh: 上變色曰：「柳渾書生，不知邊計；

translations.literal: The Emperor changed color and said, "Liu Hun is a bookish man and knows nothing of frontier strategy;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's face darkened. "Liu Hun is a scholar who knows nothing of frontier strategy;

sentences.zh: 大臣亦為此言邪！」

translations.literal: that chief ministers would also speak thus!"
translations.idiomatic: and yet my chief ministers repeat such talk!"

sentences.zh: 皆伏地頓首謝，因罷朝。

translations.literal: All prostrated themselves and knocked their heads in apology, and court was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: All prostrated themselves and kowtowed in apology, and the session was adjourned.

sentences.zh: 是夕，韓游瑰表言：「虜劫盟者，兵臨近鎮。」

translations.literal: That evening Han Yougui memorialized, saying, "The barbarians who broke the covenant—their troops press upon a nearby command."
translations.idiomatic: That evening Han Yougui submitted a memorial: "The barbarians who broke the treaty have troops at the gates of a nearby command."

sentences.zh: 上大驚，街遞其表以示渾。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly alarmed and sent the memorial by street relay to show Hun.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly alarmed and had the memorial rushed through the streets by relay to show Liu Hun.

sentences.zh: 明旦，謂渾曰：「卿書生，乃能料敵如此其審乎！」

translations.literal: At dawn he said to Hun, "You, a bookish man, could judge the enemy so accurately!"
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he said to Hun, "You—a mere scholar—and you read the enemy so clearly!"

sentences.zh: 上欲出幸，以避吐蕃，大臣諫而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to go out on a progress to avoid the Tibetans; chief ministers remonstrated and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wanted to leave the capital to escape the Tibetans; the chief ministers dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 李晟大安園多竹，復有為飛語者，云「晟伏兵大安亭，謀因倉猝為變。」

translations.literal: Li Sheng's Great Peace Garden had much bamboo; again there were flying rumors saying, "Sheng has hidden troops at Great Peace Pavilion, plotting to seize crisis and rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng's Great Peace Garden had many bamboo groves, and fresh rumors spread that "Sheng has concealed troops at Great Peace Pavilion and plans to rebel in the confusion."

sentences.zh: 晟遂伐其竹。

translations.literal: Sheng thereupon cut down the bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng then had the bamboo cut down.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，上遣中使王子恆繼詔遺尚結贊，至吐蕃境，不納而還。

translations.literal: On guiyou the Emperor sent the palace envoy Wang Ziheng with an edict and gifts for Shang Jiezan; reaching the Tibetan border, they were not received and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the Emperor dispatched the palace envoy Wang Ziheng with an edict and gifts for Shang Jiezan; at the Tibetan frontier they were refused entry and turned back.

sentences.zh: 渾瑊留屯奉天。

translations.literal: Hun Jian remained encamped at Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian stayed encamped at Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，尚結至故原州，引見崔漢衡等曰：「吾飾金械，欲械瑊以獻贊普。

translations.literal: On jiaxu Shang Jie arrived at former Yuanzhou and summoned Cui Hanheng and others, saying, "I had prepared golden fetters, intending to fetter Jian and present him to the tsenpo.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Shang Jie reached old Yuanzhou and had Cui Hanheng and the others brought before him, saying, "I had golden shackles made to bind Jian and deliver him to the tsenpo.

sentences.zh: 今失瑊，虛致公輩。」

translations.literal: Now that Jian has escaped, I have brought you all here in vain."
translations.idiomatic: Now Jian is gone, and I have dragged you here for nothing."

sentences.zh: 又謂馬燧之侄弇曰：「胡以馬為命，吾在河曲，春草未生，馬不能舉足，當是時，侍中渡河掩之，吾全軍覆沒矣！

translations.literal: He also said to Ma Sui's nephew Yan, "The Hu reckon their lives on horses. When I was at Hequ, before spring grass had sprouted the horses could not lift their feet—had the Vice Grand Councilor then crossed the river and struck us, my entire army would have been destroyed!
translations.idiomatic: He also told Ma Sui's nephew Yan, "The Hu live by their horses. At Hequ, before the spring grass came in, our horses could barely move—if the Vice Grand Councilor had crossed the river and attacked then, my whole army would have been wiped out!

sentences.zh: 所以求和，蒙侍中力。

translations.literal: The reason I sought peace was thanks to the Vice Grand Councilor's exertions.
translations.idiomatic: I owe the peace we made to the Vice Grand Councilor's efforts.

sentences.zh: 今全軍得歸，奈何拘其子孫！」

translations.literal: Now that the whole army has returned, how can you detain his sons and grandsons!"
translations.idiomatic: Now his army has come home intact—why hold his sons and kin hostage!"

sentences.zh: 命弇與宦官俱文珍、渾瑊將馬寧俱歸。

translations.literal: He ordered Yan, the eunuch Ju Wenzhen, and Hun Jian's officer Ma Ning all to return.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yan, the eunuch Ju Wenzhen, and Ma Ning, an officer under Hun Jian, all released to return.

sentences.zh: 分囚崔漢衡等於河、廓、鄯州。

translations.literal: He distributed Cui Hanheng and the others as prisoners among He, Kuo, and Shan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Cui Hanheng and the rest away as prisoners, dividing them among He, Kuo, and Shan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 上聞尚結贊之言，由是惡馬燧。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard Shang Jiezan's words, he thereupon came to dislike Ma Sui.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard what Shang Jiezan had said, he turned against Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙戌，以馬燧為司徒兼侍中，罷其副元帥、節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingxu, Ma Sui was made Grand Mentor and concurrently Vice Grand Councilor; his posts as deputy supreme commander and military governor were removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingxu, Ma Sui was appointed Grand Mentor and Vice Grand Councilor, and stripped of his roles as deputy supreme commander and military governor.

sentences.zh: 初，吐蕃尚結贊惡李晟、馬燧、渾瑊，曰：「去三人，則唐可圖也。」

translations.literal: Initially the Tibetan Shang Jiezan hated Li Sheng, Ma Sui, and Hun Jian, saying, "Remove these three men and Tang can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan had hated Li Sheng, Ma Sui, and Hun Jian, saying, "Remove these three and Tang can be taken."

sentences.zh: 於是離間李晟，因馬燧以求和，欲執渾瑊以賣燧，使並獲罪，因縱兵直犯長安，會失渾瑊而止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sowed discord against Li Sheng, sought peace through Ma Sui, and intended to seize Hun Jian to betray Sui, causing all to be condemned, then to unleash troops straight against Chang'an—but when Jian escaped he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He set out to drive Li Sheng and Ma Sui apart, use Ma Sui to sue for peace, and capture Hun Jian to implicate Sui—ruining all three so he could march on Chang'an—but Jian's escape halted the plan.

sentences.zh: 張延賞慚懼，謝病不視事。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanshang was ashamed and afraid and pleaded illness, ceasing to attend to duties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanshang, ashamed and frightened, pleaded illness and stopped coming to office.

sentences.zh: 以陝虢觀察使李泌為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Li Bi, observation commissioner of Shan-Guo, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi, commissioner overseeing Shan and Guo circuits, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 河東都虞候李自良從馬燧入朝，上欲以為河東節度使，自良固辭曰：「臣事燧日久，不欲代之為帥。」

translations.literal: Li Ziliang, chief adjutant of Hedong, followed Ma Sui to court; the Emperor wished to make him military governor of Hedong. Ziliang firmly declined, saying, "Your subject has served Sui for long and does not wish to replace him as commander."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ziliang, chief adjutant of Hedong, accompanied Ma Sui to court. The Emperor wanted to make him military governor of Hedong, but Ziliang firmly refused: "I have served under Sui for years; I do not want to step into his command."

sentences.zh: 乃以為右龍武大將軍。

translations.literal: He was therefore made General of the Right Divine Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was instead appointed General of the Right Divine Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 明日，自良入謝，上謂之曰：「卿於馬燧，存軍中事分，誠為得禮。

translations.literal: The next day Ziliang entered to give thanks; the Emperor said to him, "In your treatment of Ma Sui you preserved proper military propriety—truly fitting conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when Ziliang came to give thanks, the Emperor said, "You showed proper respect for Ma Sui's authority in the army—that was the right thing to do.

sentences.zh: 然北門之任，非卿不可。」

translations.literal: Yet the charge at the Northern Gate—no one but you can fill it."
translations.idiomatic: But the post at the Northern Gate—no one else will do."

sentences.zh: 卒以自良為河東節度使。

translations.literal: In the end Ziliang was made military governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Ziliang was appointed military governor of Hedong after all.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃之戍鹽、夏者，饋運不繼，人多病疫思歸，尚結贊遣三千騎逆之，悉焚其廬舍，毀其城，驅其民而去。

translations.literal: Tibetan garrisons at Yan and Xia could not maintain supply lines; many fell ill with pestilence and longed to return. Shang Jiezan sent three thousand horsemen to meet them; they burned all the lodges, destroyed the cities, and drove the people away.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan troops garrisoning Yan and Xia ran short of supplies; sickness spread and men yearned to go home. Shang Jiezan sent three thousand cavalry to meet them, burned every camp, razed the cities, and drove off the populace.

sentences.zh: 靈鹽節度使杜希全遣兵分守之。

translations.literal: Du Xiquan, military governor of Ling-Yan, dispatched troops to garrison the places separately.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiquan, military governor of Ling and Yan, sent troops to hold the sites in separate detachments.

sentences.zh: 韋皋以雲南頗知書，壬辰，自以書招諭之，令趣遣使入見。

translations.literal: Wei Gao judged that Yunnan was quite literate; on renchen he himself wrote letters summoning and instructing them, ordering them to hasten to send envoys to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao believed the people of Yunnan were well versed in writing; on renchen he personally wrote letters of summons and persuasion, urging them to send envoys to court without delay.

sentences.zh: 李泌初視事，壬寅，與李晟、馬燧、柳渾俱入見，上謂泌曰：「卿昔在靈武，已應為此官，卿自退讓。

translations.literal: When Li Bi first assumed office, on renyin he entered audience together with Li Sheng, Ma Sui, and Liu Hun. The Emperor said to Bi, "When you were at Lingwu you ought already to have held this post—you yourself stepped aside.
translations.idiomatic: On Li Bi's first day in office, renyin, he appeared with Li Sheng, Ma Sui, and Liu Hun. The Emperor told Bi, "At Lingwu you should already have had this rank—you declined it yourself.

sentences.zh: 朕今用卿，欲與卿有約，卿慎勿報仇，有恩者朕當為卿報之。」

translations.literal: Now that We employ you, We wish to make a pact with you: be careful not to take revenge; for those who showed you kindness We shall settle accounts on your behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Now that I am using you, I want an understanding: do not settle old scores; for anyone who was kind to you, I will see justice done.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣素奉道，不與人為仇。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your subject has long practiced the Way and bears no grudges against others.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "I have long followed the Way; I do not make enemies.

sentences.zh: 李輔國、元載皆害臣者，今自斃矣。

translations.literal: Li Fuguo and Yuan Zai both harmed your subject—they have already perished of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo and Yuan Zai both wronged me, and fate has already taken them.

sentences.zh: 素所善及有恩者，率已顯達，或多零落，臣無可報也。」

translations.literal: Those I favored and those who favored me have mostly risen to prominence, or else fallen away; your subject has nothing left to repay."
translations.idiomatic: Friends and benefactors have mostly prospered or faded away; there is nothing left for me to repay."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「雖然，有小恩者，亦當報之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Even so, for small kindnesses you should still repay them."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Even so, small favors should still be returned."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣今日亦願與陛下為約，可乎？」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your subject today also wishes to make a pact with Your Majesty—may I?"
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Today I would like a pact with Your Majesty as well—may I?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何不可！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Why not!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Of course!"

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「願陛下勿害功臣。

translations.literal: Bi said, "Your subject asks that Your Majesty not harm meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "I ask that Your Majesty never harm ministers who have served the state well.

sentences.zh: 臣受陛下厚恩，固無形跡。

translations.literal: Your subject has received Your Majesty's deep favor and naturally leaves no grounds for suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: You have shown me great trust, and I give you no cause to doubt me.

sentences.zh: 李晟、馬燧有大功於國，聞有讒之者，雖陛下必不聽，然臣今日對二人言之，欲其不自疑耳。

translations.literal: Li Sheng and Ma Sui have great merit for the state. When I hear slander against them, though Your Majesty will surely not heed it, your subject speaks openly to the two today so that they will not doubt themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng and Ma Sui have done the country great service. Rumors swirl about them; Your Majesty would never act on them, but I say this in front of both men so they need not doubt themselves.

sentences.zh: 陛下萬一害之，則宿衛之士，方鎮之臣，無不憤惋而反仄，恐中外之變不日復生也！

translations.literal: Should Your Majesty by any chance harm them, the guards of the palace and the lords of the frontier commands would all burn with indignation and unease—fearing that turmoil within and without might flare again before long!
translations.idiomatic: If harm ever came to them, the palace guards and every frontier commander would seethe with outrage and fear— and rebellion at home and abroad could follow in no time!

sentences.zh: 人臣苛蒙人主愛信則幸矣，官於何有！

translations.literal: For a subject, to be loved and trusted by the sovereign is fortune enough—what need is there for high office!
translations.idiomatic: For a minister, the sovereign's love and trust are blessing enough—what does rank matter!

sentences.zh: 臣在靈武之日，未嘗有官，而將相皆受臣指畫；

translations.literal: When your subject was at Lingwu I held no office, yet generals and chancellors all followed my direction;
translations.idiomatic: At Lingwu I held no title, yet generals and chancellors took their cues from me;

sentences.zh: 陛下以李懷光為太尉而懷光愈懼，遂至於叛。

translations.literal: when Your Majesty made Li Huai'guang Grand Marshal, Huai'guang grew only more fearful, until he rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: when you made Li Huai'guang Grand Marshal, he grew only more terrified, until he rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 此皆陛下所親見也。

translations.literal: All this Your Majesty saw with your own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: You saw all of that yourself.

sentences.zh: 今晟、燧富貴已足，苟陛下坦然待之，使其自保無虞，國家有事則出從征伐，無事則入奉朝請，何樂如之！

translations.literal: Now Sheng and Sui have wealth and rank enough; if Your Majesty treats them openly, letting them keep themselves without worry—when the state has business they go out to campaign, when there is none they come in to attend court—what could be more joyous!
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and Sui already have wealth and honor enough. Treat them plainly, let them live without fear—when the realm needs them they ride to war, when it does not they attend court. What could be better!

sentences.zh: 故臣願陛下勿以二臣功大而忌之，二臣勿以位高而自疑，則天下永無事矣。」

translations.literal: Therefore your subject asks Your Majesty not to envy the two ministers for their great merit, and the two ministers not to doubt themselves for their high rank—then the realm will never know trouble.
translations.idiomatic: So I beg Your Majesty not to resent them for their achievements, and beg them not to suspect you because of their rank—then the empire will stay at peace.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕始聞卿言，聳然不知所謂。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "When I first heard your words I was startled and did not know what you meant.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "When I first heard you I was shocked—I did not understand.

sentences.zh: 及聽卿剖析，乃知社稷之至計也！

translations.literal: After hearing your analysis I know this is the supreme strategy for the altars of state!
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have explained it, I see this is the vital policy for the realm!

sentences.zh: 朕謹當書紳，二大臣亦當共保之。」

translations.literal: We shall diligently inscribe it on Our sash, and the two great ministers must likewise preserve it together."
translations.idiomatic: I will write it on my sash and keep it; the two of you must uphold it with me."

sentences.zh: 晟、燧皆起，泣謝。

translations.literal: Sheng and Sui both rose and wept their thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng and Ma Sui both stood, weeping, and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 上因謂泌曰：「自今凡軍旅糧儲事，卿主之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then said to Bi, "From today all military grain and stores shall be under your charge.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then told Bi, "From now on you will oversee all army grain and supplies.

sentences.zh: 吏、禮委延賞，刑法委渾。」

translations.literal: Personnel and rites delegate to Yanshang; penal law delegate to Hun."
translations.idiomatic: Leave personnel and ritual to Yanshang, and criminal law to Hun."

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Bi said, "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "That cannot be.

sentences.zh: 陛下不以臣不才，使待罪宰相。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, not deeming your subject unworthy, has made me a chancellor bearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, despite my shortcomings, has made me chancellor.

sentences.zh: 宰相之職，不可分也。

translations.literal: The chancellor's office cannot be divided.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor's role cannot be split up.

sentences.zh: 非如給事則有吏過、兵過，舍人則有六押，至於宰相，天下之事鹹共平章。

translations.literal: It is unlike the Secretariat Receptionist, who has oversight of civil and military memorials, or the Drafting Secretary with his six seals—as chancellor, all affairs under Heaven are deliberated together.
translations.idiomatic: A receptionist handles civil or military paperwork; a drafting secretary holds six seals—but a chancellor deliberates on every affair under Heaven together with the throne.

sentences.zh: 若各有所主，是乃有司，非宰相也。」

translations.literal: If each had his own domain, these would be mere functionaries, not chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: If each minister owned a separate portfolio, they would be clerks, not chancellors.

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「朕適失辭，卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "We misspoke just now; your view is correct."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed. "I spoke hastily—you are right."

sentences.zh: 泌請復所減州、縣官。

translations.literal: Bi requested restoration of the prefectural and county posts that had been cut.
translations.idiomatic: Bi asked to restore the prefectural and county posts that had been abolished.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「置吏以為人也，今戶口減於承平之時三分之二，而吏員更增，可乎！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Officials are appointed for the people; household registers are now two-thirds below the age of peace, yet the roster of clerks has grown—how can that be!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "We appoint officials to serve the people. Households are down by two-thirds from peacetime, yet the bureaucracy keeps growing—how is that acceptable!

sentences.zh: 對曰：「戶口雖減，而事多於承平且十倍，吏得無增乎！

translations.literal: He replied, "Though households have declined, affairs are more than ten times what they were in peaceful times—how could clerks not increase!
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "Households may be fewer, but the workload is ten times what it was in peace—how could staff not grow!

sentences.zh: 且所減皆有職事而冗官不減，此所以為未當也。

translations.literal: Moreover what was cut all had real duties while redundant posts were not reduced—that is why the policy was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, you eliminated posts that did real work while leaving idle sinecures untouched—that is why the cuts were wrong.

sentences.zh: 至德以來置額外官，敵正官三分之一，若聽使計日得資然後停，加兩選授同類正員官。

translations.literal: Since Zhide extra posts have been established equaling one-third of regular posts; if we let them accrue pay by the day and then stop, and after two selection cycles grant them regular posts of the same class—
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhide era we have filled one-third as many extra posts as regular ones. Let those extras draw daily pay until they are phased out, then after two promotion cycles grant them regular rank in the same track—

sentences.zh: 如此，則不惟不怨，兼使之喜矣。」

translations.literal: thus not only would there be no resentment—they would even rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: —and they will not merely accept it; they will welcome it.

sentences.zh: 又請諸王未出閣者不除府官，上皆從之。

translations.literal: He also requested that princes who had not yet left the palace not be given staff appointments; the Emperor agreed to all.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that princes who had not yet been given households outside the palace not receive full staff appointments; the Emperor agreed to everything.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔先所減官，並復故。

translations.literal: On yimao an edict ordered all previously cut posts restored.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao an edict restored every post that had been cut.

sentences.zh: 初，張延賞在西川，與東川節度使李叔明有隙。

translations.literal: Initially when Zhang Yanshang was in Xichuan he had a grudge against Li Shuming, military governor of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Zhang Yanshang served in Xichuan, he had fallen out with Li Shuming, military governor of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 上入駱谷，值霖雨，道塗隊伍滑，衛士多亡歸朱泚，叔明之子升及郭子儀之子曙，令狐彰之子建等六人，恐有奸人危乘輿，相與嚙臂為盟，著行滕、釘革奚，更鞚上馬以至梁州，他人皆不得近。

translations.literal: When the Emperor entered Luogu Pass, heavy rains made the roads and columns slip; many guards fled back to Zhu Ci. Li Shuming's son Sheng, Guo Ziyi's son Shu, Linghu Zhang's son Jian, and three others, fearing villains might endanger the imperial carriage, bit their arms in covenant, put on leg guards and nailed leather soles, helped the Emperor remount and escorted him to Liangzhou—no one else could approach.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor fled through Luogu Pass, torrential rain turned the road to mud and columns slid; many guards deserted to Zhu Ci. Li Shuming's son Sheng, Guo Ziyi's son Shu, Linghu Zhang's son Jian, and three companions, fearing assassins might reach the carriage, bit their arms in blood oath, strapped on leg guards and spiked soles, lifted the Emperor back onto his horse, and escorted him all the way to Liangzhou—keeping everyone else at a distance.

sentences.zh: 及還長安，上皆以為禁衛將軍，寵遇甚厚。

translations.literal: When they returned to Chang'an the Emperor made them all imperial guard generals with very generous favor.
translations.idiomatic: After the return to Chang'an the Emperor made them all palace guard generals and treated them with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 張延賞知升私出入郜國大長公主第，密以白上。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanshang learned Sheng was privately visiting the Princess of Guo State the Elder and secretly reported it to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanshang discovered that Sheng was secretly visiting the Elder Princess of Guo and quietly informed the Emperor.
