sentences.zh: 上謂李泌曰：「郜國已老，升年少，何為如是！

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Li Bi, "The Princess of Guo is already old and Sheng is young—why act thus!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to Li Bi, "The Princess of Guo is elderly and Sheng is young—why would they carry on like this!

sentences.zh: 殆必有故，卿宜察之。」

translations.literal: There must be a reason; you should investigate."
translations.idiomatic: There must be more to it. Look into this for me."

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「此必有欲動搖東宮者。

translations.literal: Bi said, "Someone must be trying to shake the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Someone is trying to undermine the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 誰為陛下言之？」

translations.literal: Who told Your Majesty this?"
translations.idiomatic: Who brought this to Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿勿問，第為朕察之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Do not ask; simply investigate for Us."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Never mind who—just investigate."

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「必延賞也。」

translations.literal: Bi said, "It must be Yanshang."
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "It has to be Yanshang."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何以知之？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "How do you know?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked, "How can you tell?"

sentences.zh: 泌具為上言二人之隙，且曰：「升承恩顧，典禁兵，延賞無以中傷，而郜國乃太子蕭妃之母也，故欲以此陷之耳。」

translations.literal: Bi fully related to the Emperor the rift between the two, adding, "Sheng enjoys imperial favor and commands the guard; Yanshang had no way to slander him—but the Princess of Guo is the Crown Prince's mother through Consort Xiao, so he wishes to trap him with this."
translations.idiomatic: Bi laid out the feud between Yanshang and Shuming and said, "Sheng enjoys the Emperor's trust and commands the guard—Yanshang could not touch him directly. But the Princess of Guo is the Crown Prince's mother-in-law through Consort Xiao, so Yanshang means to entangle Sheng with scandal."

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「是也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "Exactly."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed. "Exactly right."

sentences.zh: 泌因請除升它官，勿令宿衛以遠嫌。

translations.literal: Bi then requested that Sheng be given another post and not remain on guard duty to keep distance from suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Bi then asked that Sheng be transferred to another post and removed from palace guard duty to avoid suspicion.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以升為詹事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Sheng was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Sheng was appointed Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 郜國，肅宗之女也。

translations.literal: The Princess of Guo was a daughter of Emperor Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Guo was a daughter of Emperor Suzong.

sentences.zh: 甲子，割振武之綏、銀二州，以右羽林將軍韓潭為夏、綏、銀節度使，帥神策之士五千、朔方、河東之士三千鎮夏州。

translations.literal: On jiazi Sui and Yin prefectures were split from Zhenwu; Han Tan, General of the Right Feathered Forest, was made military governor of Xia, Sui, and Yin, leading five thousand Shence troops and three thousand from Shuofang and Hedong to garrison Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Sui and Yin were detached from Zhenwu; Han Tan, general of the Right Imperial Guard, became military governor of Xia, Sui, and Yin, commanding five thousand Shence troops plus three thousand from Shuofang and Hedong to hold Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時關東防秋兵大集，國用不充。

translations.literal: At that time eastern-pass defense troops for autumn were massing; state revenues were insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern frontier troops were assembling for the autumn defense, and the treasury could not keep up.

sentences.zh: 李泌奏：「自變兩稅法以來，籓鎮、州、縣多違法聚斂。

translations.literal: Li Bi memorialized, "Since the reform of the two-tax system, circuit armies and prefectures have often unlawfully amassed levies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi submitted a memorial: "Since the two-tax reform, military governors and local officials have often collected taxes outside the law.

sentences.zh: 繼以朱泚之亂，爭榷率、征罰以為軍資，點募自防。

translations.literal: Following Zhu Ci's rebellion they competed in monopolies, assessments, and fines to fund armies and mustered troops for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Ci's rebellion they raced to impose monopolies, surcharges, and penalties to fund armies and conscript men for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 泚既平，自懼違法，匿不敢言。

translations.literal: Once Ci was suppressed they feared their violations and hid them, not daring to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhu Ci was gone they were afraid to admit their abuses and kept silent.

sentences.zh: 請遣使以詔旨赦其罪，但令革正，自非於法應留使、留州之外，悉輸京師。

translations.literal: Your subject asks to send envoys with an edict pardoning their crimes, requiring only correction—except where law permits retention for commissioners or prefectures, all should be sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys with an edict pardoning past offenses and requiring only reform. Aside from what the law allows regions and commissioners to retain, everything else should flow to the capital.

sentences.zh: 其官典逋負，可征者征之，難征者釋之，以示寬大。

translations.literal: For officials' outstanding debts, collect where collection is feasible; release where it is hard—thus showing magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: For debts owed by local officials, collect what can reasonably be collected and write off the rest, as a sign of leniency.

sentences.zh: 敢有隱沒者，重設告賞之科而罪之。」

translations.literal: Whoever dares to conceal or embezzle shall have the informant-reward statutes reinstated and be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who concealed or withheld funds would face reinstated whistleblower rewards and criminal penalties."

sentences.zh: 上喜曰：「卿策甚長，然立法太寬，恐所得無幾！」

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure, "Your plan is very thorough, yet the law you propose is too lenient—I fear the yield will be slight!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said warmly, "Your plan is far-reaching, but the law is too lenient. I'm afraid we won't collect much!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「茲事臣固熟思之，寬則獲多而速，急則獲少而遲。

translations.literal: Bi replied, "On this matter Your subject has indeed thought it through carefully: if lenient, more will be obtained quickly; if harsh, less will be obtained slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "I have given this much thought. Leniency brings in more revenue, faster; harshness brings in less, and slowly.

sentences.zh: 蓋以寬則人喜於免罪而樂輸，急則競為蔽匿，非推鞫不能得其實，財不足濟今日之急而皆入於奸吏矣。」

translations.literal: For if lenient, people rejoice at escaping punishment and gladly pay; if harsh, they compete to conceal and hide—without interrogation one cannot get the truth, and the funds will not suffice for today's urgency but will all go to corrupt officials."
translations.idiomatic: Under leniency people gladly pay rather than face punishment; under harshness they conceal everything, and only torture will extract the truth—the treasury still won't meet today's need, and the money will end up in corrupt officials' hands."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Excellent!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Good!

sentences.zh: 以度支員外郎元友直為河南、江、淮南句勘兩稅錢帛使。

translations.literal: Yuan Youzhi, Vice Director of the Revenue Office, was appointed commissioner for line-item audit of two-tax money and silk in Henan, Jiang, and Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Youzhi, vice director of the treasury, was appointed to audit two-tax revenues in Henan, Jiang, and Huainan.

sentences.zh: 初，河、隴既沒於吐蕃，自天寶以來，安西、北庭奏事及西域使人在長安者，歸路既絕，人馬皆仰給於鴻臚。

translations.literal: Initially, after the He-Long region had fallen to Tibet, since the Tianbao era Anxi and Beiting memorialists and Western Region envoys in Chang'an, their return routes having been cut off, men and horses all depended on the Court of Dependencies for support.
translations.idiomatic: After the He-Long region fell to Tibet, envoys from Anxi and Beiting and Western Region delegates stranded in Chang'an since the Tianbao era had no way home; the Court of Dependencies supplied men and horses.

sentences.zh: 禮賓委府、縣供之，於度支受直。

translations.literal: The Protocol Office delegated to prefectures and counties to supply them, receiving payment from the Revenue Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Protocol Office had prefectures and counties provide for them and was reimbursed by the treasury.

sentences.zh: 度支不時付直，長安市肆不勝其弊。

translations.literal: The Revenue Office did not pay promptly; Chang'an's markets could not bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury paid late, and Chang'an merchants could not bear the strain.

sentences.zh: 李泌知胡客留長安久者，或四十餘年，皆有妻子，買田宅，舉質取利，安居不欲歸，命檢括胡客有田宅者停其給。

translations.literal: Li Bi knew that among foreign guests long resident in Chang'an, some for forty-odd years, all had wives and children, bought fields and houses, pawned property for profit, lived at ease and did not wish to return—he ordered an audit of foreign guests possessing fields and houses to stop their provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi learned that some foreign guests had lived in Chang'an for forty years or more, taken wives, bought land, and lent at interest—they had settled in and did not want to leave. He ordered an audit and cut off supplies to any foreign guest who owned property.

sentences.zh: 凡得四千人，將停其給。

translations.literal: Altogether four thousand persons were found; their provisions were about to be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The audit found four thousand people whose stipends were to be cut off.

sentences.zh: 胡客皆詣政府訴之，泌曰：「此皆從來宰相之過，豈有外國朝貢使者留京師數十年不聽歸乎！

translations.literal: The foreign guests all went to the government to complain. Bi said, "These are all past chancellors' errors—how can foreign tribute envoys be kept in the capital for decades without being allowed to return!
translations.idiomatic: The foreign guests all petitioned the government. Bi said, "This is the fault of chancellors past—what envoy from abroad is kept in the capital for decades and never sent home?

sentences.zh: 今當假道於回紇，或自海道各遣歸國，有不願歸者，當於鴻臚自陳，授以職位，給俸祿為唐臣。

translations.literal: Now they should be sent back to their countries via the Uyghurs as a pass-through, or by sea route each to his own land. Those unwilling to return should declare themselves at the Court of Dependencies, be given offices, and receive salaries as subjects of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Send them home by way of the Uyghurs, or by sea—each to his own country. Those who wish to stay should register with the Court of Dependencies, take office, and serve the Tang on salary.

sentences.zh: 人生當乘時展用，豈可終身客死邪！」

translations.literal: In life one ought to seize the season and display one's talents—how can one die a guest abroad for a lifetime!"
translations.idiomatic: A man should make his mark while he can—who wants to die a stranger in a foreign land?

sentences.zh: 於是胡客無一人願歸者，泌皆分隸神策兩軍，王子、使者為散兵馬使或押牙，餘皆為卒，禁旅益壯。

translations.literal: Thereupon not one foreign guest wished to return; Bi assigned them all to the two Shence armies—princes and envoys as scattered cavalry officers or guard lieutenants, the rest as soldiers—the palace guard grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Not one foreign guest chose to leave. Bi enrolled them all in the two Shence armies—princes and envoys as cavalry officers or guard lieutenants, the rest as rank-and-file—the imperial guard grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚所給胡客才十餘人，歲省度支錢五十萬緡，市人皆喜。

translations.literal: The foreign guests supplied by the Court of Dependencies numbered only a dozen or so; yearly five hundred thousand strings of Revenue Office funds were saved, and market people were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Dependencies now supported barely a dozen foreign guests, saving five hundred thousand strings a year—and the merchants rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 上復問泌以復府兵之策。

translations.literal: The emperor again asked Bi about the strategy for restoring the militia system.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again asked Bi how to restore the militia system.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「今歲征關東卒戍京西者十七萬人，計歲食粟二百四萬斛。

translations.literal: Bi replied, "This year the soldiers conscripted from the eastern passes to garrison the western capital number one hundred seventy thousand; calculating annual grain consumption at two million four hundred thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "This year we have conscripted one hundred seventy thousand men from east of the passes to garrison the western capital. They consume two million four hundred thousand hu of grain annually.

sentences.zh: 今粟斗直錢百五十，為錢三百六萬緡。

translations.literal: Now grain per peck is worth one hundred fifty cash, making three million six hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: At one hundred fifty cash per peck, that comes to three million six hundred thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 國家比遭饑亂，經費不充，就使有錢，亦無粟可糴，未暇議復府兵也。」

translations.literal: The state has recently suffered famine and rebellion; funds are insufficient. Even if there were money, there is no grain to purchase—the time has not come to discuss restoring the militia."
translations.idiomatic: The realm has just endured famine and rebellion; funds are thin. Even with money in hand, there is no grain to buy—we cannot discuss restoring the militia yet."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然將奈何？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Then what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then what do we do?

sentences.zh: 亟減戍卒歸之，何如？」

translations.literal: Quickly reduce the garrison troops and send them back—how about that?"
translations.idiomatic: What if we cut the garrisons and send the men home at once?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下誠能用臣之言，可以不減戍卒，不擾百姓，糧食皆足，粟麥日賤，府兵亦成。」

translations.literal: Bi replied, "If Your Majesty truly can use Your subject's words, you can avoid reducing garrison troops, avoid disturbing the people, have grain fully sufficient, millet and wheat daily cheaper, and the militia system also accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "If Your Majesty will follow my advice, you need not cut the garrisons or burden the people. Grain will be ample, millet and wheat will grow cheaper by the day—and the militia can be restored as well."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「果能如是，何為不用！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "If it can truly be thus, why not use it!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If it really works that way, why wouldn't we do it!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此須急為之，過旬日則不及矣。

translations.literal: Bi replied, "This must be done urgently—past ten days it will be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "This must be done at once. Wait ten days and the opportunity will be gone.

sentences.zh: 今吐蕃久居原、蘭之間，以牛運糧，糧盡，占無所用，請發左藏惡繒染為彩纈，因党項以市之，每頭不過二三匹，計十八萬匹，可致六萬餘頭。

translations.literal: Now the Tibetans have long been stationed between Yuan and Lan, using oxen to transport grain. When the grain is exhausted they are useless. Your subject requests issuing inferior silk from the Left Treasury, dyed into colorful fabrics, and trading through the Tangut—for each head no more than two or three bolts; estimating one hundred eighty thousand bolts, more than sixty thousand head can be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans have long held Yuan and Lan, hauling grain with oxen. When the grain runs out, the oxen are worthless. Issue the inferior silk from the Left Treasury, dye it into patterned fabrics, and trade through the Tangut—two or three bolts per head. One hundred eighty thousand bolts should buy more than sixty thousand oxen.

sentences.zh: 又命諸冶鑄農器糴麥種，分賜沿邊軍鎮，募戍卒，耕荒田而種之，約明年麥熟倍償其種，其餘據時價五分增一，官為糴之。

translations.literal: He also ordered all smithies to cast farm tools and purchase wheat seed, distribute them to garrison towns along the border, recruit garrison soldiers to cultivate wasteland and plant it, stipulating that when wheat ripened the next year they would repay double the seed; as for the remainder, the state would purchase it at the current market price plus one-fifth.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered smithies to cast farm tools and buy wheat seed, distributed them to frontier garrisons, and recruited garrison troops to break wasteland. They would repay double the seed after next year's harvest; the government would buy the rest at market price plus twenty percent.

sentences.zh: 來春種禾亦如之。

translations.literal: The following spring planting millet would be treated the same way.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring they would plant millet on the same terms.

sentences.zh: 關中土沃而久荒，所收必厚。

translations.literal: Guanzhong's soil is fertile and long fallow—the harvest will surely be abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong's soil is rich and long untilled—the yields will be heavy.

sentences.zh: 戍卒獲利，耕者浸多。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers would profit; cultivators would gradually increase.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison soldiers would profit, and more and more would take up farming.

sentences.zh: 邊地居人至少，軍士月食官糧，粟麥無所售，其價必賤，名為增價，實比今歲所減多矣。」

translations.literal: Border lands have at least some inhabitants; soldiers monthly eat official grain—millet and wheat would have nowhere to be sold, and prices must be cheap. Though called a price increase, in reality it would be more reduction than this year's."
translations.idiomatic: Even where the frontier has a few civilians, soldiers draw monthly rations—millet and wheat will have no buyers, and prices will fall. Though we call it a price increase, we'll actually save more than this year's cuts."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Excellent!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Good!

sentences.zh: 即命行之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered it carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it implemented at once.

sentences.zh: 泌又言：「邊地官多闕，請募人入粟以補之，可足今歲之糧。」

translations.literal: Bi further said, "Border posts have many vacancies. Your subject requests recruiting people to contribute grain to fill them—it can suffice for this year's grain."
translations.idiomatic: Bi added, "Many frontier posts are vacant. Let people buy offices with grain contributions—that will cover this year's needs."

sentences.zh: 上亦從之，因問曰：「卿言府兵亦集，如何？」

translations.literal: The emperor also agreed, and asked, "You said the militia would also be gathered—how?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, then asked, "You said the militia could be restored too—how?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「戍卒因屯田致富，則安於其土，不復思歸。

translations.literal: Bi replied, "When garrison soldiers grow rich through frontier farming, they will be content on their land and no longer think of returning.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "Once garrison soldiers grow wealthy from tuntian, they'll settle on the land and stop thinking of going home.

sentences.zh: 舊制，戍卒三年而代，及其將滿，下令有願留者，即以所開田為永業。

translations.literal: Under the old system, garrison soldiers were replaced after three years. When their term was nearly complete, an order was issued: those willing to stay would take the land they had opened as permanent property.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, garrison soldiers rotated every three years. Near the end of their term, those who wished to stay would receive the land they had cleared as permanent holdings.

sentences.zh: 家人原來來者，本貫給長牒續食而遣之。

translations.literal: Family members who had originally come along—from their native registry long travel documents were issued, provisions continued, and they were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Family members who had come with them would receive long travel passes from their home districts, continued rations, and be sent home.

sentences.zh: 據應募之數，移報本道，雖河朔諸帥得免更代之煩，亦喜聞矣。

translations.literal: According to the number who volunteered, reports would be sent to the home circuits—even the Hebei warlords, exempted from the trouble of rotation, would also be glad to hear it.
translations.idiomatic: Report the numbers who volunteer to their home circuits. Even the warlords of Hebei, spared the burden of rotations, would welcome the news.

sentences.zh: 不過數番，則戍卒皆土著，乃悉以府兵之法理之，是變關中之疲弊為富強也。」

translations.literal: Within a few rotations the garrison soldiers would all be native settlers; then the militia methods would fully govern them—thus transforming Guanzhong's exhaustion and weakness into strength and wealth."
translations.idiomatic: After a few rotations the garrison troops would all be permanent settlers, and we'd restore the full militia system—turning Guanzhong's exhaustion into prosperity."

sentences.zh: 上喜曰：「如此，天下無復事矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure, "Thus, under Heaven there will be no further affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said delightedly, "Then the realm will have nothing left to worry about."

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「未也。

translations.literal: Bi said, "Not yet.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Not yet.

sentences.zh: 臣能不用中國之兵使吐蕃自困。」

translations.literal: Your subject can, without using China's troops, make Tibet trouble itself."
translations.idiomatic: I can wear Tibet down without deploying a single Chinese soldier."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「計將安出？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What plan will emerge?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What's the plan?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣未敢言之，俟麥禾有效，然後可議也。」

translations.literal: Bi replied, "Your subject dares not speak of it yet—wait until the wheat and millet plan proves effective, then it can be discussed."
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "I'm not ready to say yet. Let's see whether the grain scheme works—then we can discuss it.

sentences.zh: 上固問，不對。

translations.literal: The emperor pressed him, but Bi did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed him, but Bi would not reply.

sentences.zh: 泌意欲結回紇、大食、雲南與共圖吐蕃，令吐蕃所備者多。

translations.literal: Bi intended to ally with the Uyghurs, the Arabs, and Yunnan jointly to scheme against Tibet, causing Tibet to need to prepare on many fronts.
translations.idiomatic: Bi meant to ally the Uyghurs, Arabia, and Yunnan against Tibet, forcing Tibet to guard many fronts.

sentences.zh: 知上素恨回紇，恐聞之不悅，並屯田之議不行，故不肯言。

translations.literal: Knowing the emperor had long resented the Uyghurs, he feared that hearing this he would be displeased and the tuntian proposal would not be carried out, and therefore was unwilling to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing how much the emperor hated the Uyghurs, Bi feared the tuntian plan would die if the emperor took offense—so he kept silent.

sentences.zh: 既而戍卒應募，願耕屯田者什五六。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter among garrison soldiers who volunteered, five or six tenths wished to farm tuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, fifty or sixty percent of garrison volunteers signed up for tuntian farming.

sentences.zh: 壬申，賜駱元光姓名李元諒。

translations.literal: On renshen, Luo Yuanguang was granted the personal name Li Yuanliang.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Luo Yuanguang was granted the surname Li and the personal name Yuanliang.

sentences.zh: 左僕射、同平章事張延賞薨。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director and Fellow Grand Councilor Zhang Yanshang died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanshang, Left Vice Director and Fellow Grand Councilor, died.

translations.idiomatic: CATEGORY: Zizhi Tongjian (Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance)
